curriculumGuide.title: Before Unit 1: Hangul and sound
curriculumGuide.goal: Read Korean syllable blocks accurately before relying on romanization.
points: Know that each block is built from initial consonant, vowel, and optional final consonant.
Practice final consonants because they affect the next syllable.
Use romanization as support, then move your eyes back to Hangul and audio.
curriculumGuide.task: Read five phrases aloud, then play the audio and compare.

curriculumGuide.title: Every chapter: vocabulary, grammar, conversation
curriculumGuide.goal: Move from word to pattern to real exchange.
points: Vocabulary: learn the chunk and one sentence frame.
Grammar: learn the particle or ending that makes the sentence work.
Conversation: say the item inside a mini dialogue, then change one word.
curriculumGuide.task: Open one word card, one grammar item, and one expression before the final task.

curriculumGuide.title: Beginner functions to cover
curriculumGuide.goal: Build survival communication, not only translation.
points: Ordering food, buying items, asking price, and paying.
Asking location, transportation, classroom help, and inviting.
curriculumGuide.task: After each chapter, say one sentence you could use in Korea today.

curriculumGuide.title: Culture and politeness layer
curriculumGuide.goal: Choose Korean that fits the person and situation.
points: Default to 해요체 with adults, staff, teachers, and strangers.
Notice titles and honorific direction before casual speech.
Learn signs and staff instructions even if you do not use them often yourself.
curriculumGuide.task: For each expression, decide whether it is casual, polite everyday, or formal/service speech.

chapters.title: Hangul, Syllable Blocks, And Sound
chapters.goal: Understand how Hangul blocks work and use romanization only as a temporary helper.
chapters.scenario: First self-study session before speaking.

dialogue.speaker: Tutor
dialogue.ko: 여기 한글 글자 하나 볼까요? 한이에요.
dialogue.romanization: yeogi hangeul geulja hana bolkkayo? hanieyo.
dialogue.en: Shall we look at one Hangul character here? It is 한.

dialogue.speaker: Learner
dialogue.en: Han... please say it slowly.

dialogue.speaker: Tutor
dialogue.ko: 한. ㅎ, ㅏ, ㄴ이 같이 있어요.
dialogue.romanization: han. hieut, a, nieuni gachi isseoyo.
dialogue.en: Han. ㅎ, ㅏ, and ㄴ are together.

dialogue.speaker: Learner
dialogue.en: Ah, it is 한.

dialogue.speaker: Tutor
dialogue.ko: 맞아요. 로마자는 나중에 보고, 한글을 먼저 읽어요.
dialogue.romanization: majayo. romajaneun najunge bogo, hangeureul meonjeo ilgeoyo.
dialogue.en: Right. Look at romanization later, and read the Hangul first.

chapters.guidedPractice: Break 한글 into blocks, read each block from Hangul, then check romanization only after you try.
chapters.realLifeTask: Ask a Korean-speaking friend or tutor to say one phrase slowly and repeat it back.
chapters.friendPractice: Friend says three phrases from this chapter. Learner points to the Hangul and repeats.
chapters.review: Can you explain that 한 is ㅎ + ㅏ + ㄴ, read a simple block, and use romanization only as a helper?

beginnerGuide.title: What a complete beginner should notice
beginnerGuide.body: Hangul is not an alphabet written in a line like English. Korean letters are grouped into square syllable blocks, so 한 is one spoken chunk made from ㅎ, ㅏ, and ㄴ.

beginnerGuide.title: How to study this chapter
beginnerGuide.body: Look at the Hangul first, try to read it, then use romanization only to check. If you start from romanization, you will build English pronunciation habits that are hard to undo.

beginnerGuide.title: Minimum outcome
beginnerGuide.body: You do not need perfect pronunciation yet. You should be able to point to a block, name its parts, and repeat a short phrase after listening.

checkpoints: I can explain that 한 is ㅎ + ㅏ + ㄴ.
I can read a short phrase from Hangul before checking romanization.
I know romanization is a helper, not Korean spelling.

chapters.title: Greetings And Self-Introduction
chapters.goal: Greet, thank, apologize, answer yes/no, and introduce your name politely.
chapters.scenario: First class, first meeting, store, or language exchange.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.en: Hello. What is your name?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.en: Hello. I am Hana.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.en: I am Minjun. Nice to meet you.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.en: Nice to meet you.

chapters.guidedPractice: Replace the name in 저는 하나예요 with your own name, then add one greeting and one closing.
chapters.realLifeTask: Introduce yourself in three polite sentences.
chapters.friendPractice: Friend asks 이름이 뭐예요? Learner answers with 저는 ___예요.
chapters.review: Can you greet, say your name, thank someone, and close the conversation politely?

beginnerGuide.title: Why greetings come before grammar
beginnerGuide.body: A beginner needs phrases that work immediately. 안녕하세요, 감사합니다, 죄송합니다, 네, and 아니요 let you participate politely before you can build long sentences.

beginnerGuide.title: Politeness first
beginnerGuide.body: Use polite everyday Korean until the other person clearly uses casual speech with you. This course treats 해요체 and polite chunks as your default safety zone.

beginnerGuide.title: Your first personal sentence
beginnerGuide.body: 저는 ___예요 is not just translation practice. It teaches 은/는 as “as for me,” which becomes the base for many later sentences.

checkpoints: I can greet and thank someone without reading English.
I can say 저는 ___예요 with my own name.
I can choose 감사합니다 when I want to sound safer or more formal.

chapters.title: Noun Sentences: N이에요/예요 And 은/는
chapters.goal: Say what something is and set the topic with 은/는.
chapters.scenario: Names, jobs, places, and basic identity.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.en: What is this?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.en: This is a menu.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.en: I am Minsu. I am a student.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.en: I am Hana. I am an office worker.

chapters.guidedPractice: Make three N이에요/예요 sentences: your name, your role, and one object.
chapters.realLifeTask: Point to two things around you and say what they are.
chapters.friendPractice: Friend points to an object. Learner asks 이건 뭐예요? and repeats the answer.
chapters.review: Can you choose 이에요 vs 예요 and use 저는 naturally?

beginnerGuide.title: The first sentence engine
beginnerGuide.body: N이에요/예요 lets you say what something is. This is the noun-sentence engine for names, jobs, objects, places, and simple identity.

beginnerGuide.title: Topic marker in plain English
beginnerGuide.body: 은/는 marks what we are talking about. In 저는 학생이에요, Korean first says “as for me,” then gives the information.

beginnerGuide.title: Do not over-translate particles
beginnerGuide.body: Particles often do not become separate English words. Learn the Korean frame and the sentence job, not a one-word English translation.

checkpoints: I can choose 이에요 after a final consonant and 예요 after a vowel.
I can ask 이건 뭐예요?
I can explain 은/는 as topic or contrast.

chapters.title: Existence And Possession: 있어요/없어요 And 이/가
chapters.goal: Say what exists, what you have, and what is missing.
chapters.scenario: Reservations, time, money, bathrooms, and problems.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.en: Do you have a reservation?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.en: No, I do not have a reservation. Is there a seat?

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.en: Yes, there is a seat. There is no problem.

chapters.guidedPractice: Practice 시간이 있어요, 시간이 없어요, 예약이 있어요, 예약이 없어요.
chapters.realLifeTask: Ask if there is a bathroom or reservation, then answer yes/no.
chapters.friendPractice: Friend asks 시간이 있어요? Learner answers with 있어요 or 없어요 and one reason.
chapters.review: Can you use 이/가 with 있어요 and 없어요?

beginnerGuide.title: Existence covers more than “there is”
beginnerGuide.body: 있어요 and 없어요 also mean “I have” and “I do not have.” 시간이 있어요 can mean “there is time” or “I have time.”

beginnerGuide.title: Why 이/가 appears here
beginnerGuide.body: The thing that exists, does not exist, hurts, or appears is usually marked with 이/가: 시간이 있어요, 문제가 없어요, 머리가 아파요.

beginnerGuide.title: Survival value
beginnerGuide.body: This chapter gives you high-frequency travel and daily phrases: 예약이 있어요, 시간이 없어요, 화장실이 있어요?

checkpoints: I can say I have time and I do not have time.
I can ask whether something exists with 있어요?
I do not use 을/를 for the thing that exists.

chapters.title: Daily Actions: Present Tense And 을/를
chapters.goal: Say what you do every day and what object receives the action.
chapters.scenario: Meals, study, work, reading, writing, and daily routine.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.en: Do you eat breakfast?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.en: Yes, I eat breakfast. I drink coffee.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.en: Do you study Korean?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.en: Yes, I study Korean. I read books.

chapters.guidedPractice: Make three present-tense sentences with 을/를, then make one negative sentence.
chapters.realLifeTask: Say three things you do today and one thing you do not do.
chapters.friendPractice: Friend asks 뭐 해요? Learner answers with one object sentence.
chapters.review: Can you use 먹어요, 마셔요, 공부해요, and 안 해요 naturally?

beginnerGuide.title: From words to actions
beginnerGuide.body: This chapter turns verbs into simple sentences: 밥을 먹어요, 커피를 마셔요, 한국어를 공부해요. The object marker 을/를 shows what receives the action.

beginnerGuide.title: Particle dropping comes later
beginnerGuide.body: Koreans often drop 을/를 in speech, but beginners should first understand the full frame. Once the structure is clear, natural short speech becomes easier.

beginnerGuide.title: Negatives start here
beginnerGuide.body: 안 먹어요 and 공부 안 해요 show the everyday short negative. This means “I do not do it,” not necessarily “I cannot.”

checkpoints: I can make a present-tense sentence with an object.
I can use 을 after a consonant and 를 after a vowel.
I can make a short negative with 안.

chapters.title: Places And Time: 에 And 에서
chapters.goal: Say where you go, where you are, where actions happen, and when things happen.
chapters.scenario: School, work, home, appointments, and movement.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.en: Where are you going?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.en: I go to school.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.en: What do you do at school?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.en: I study at school.

chapters.guidedPractice: Contrast 학교에 가요 with 학교에서 공부해요. Do not mix destination and action place.
chapters.realLifeTask: Say where you are, where you go, and where you study or work.
chapters.friendPractice: Friend asks 어디에 가요? and 어디에서 공부해요? Learner answers both.
chapters.review: Can you choose 에 vs 에서 in simple sentences?

beginnerGuide.title: The 에 / 에서 split
beginnerGuide.body: 에 points to destination, time, or where something exists. 에서 marks where an action happens. 학교에 가요 and 학교에서 공부해요 are different for a reason.

beginnerGuide.title: Movement vs action
beginnerGuide.body: If the verb is 가다 or 오다, think destination: 에. If the verb is 공부하다, 일하다, 먹다, 기다리다, or 사다, think action place: 에서.

beginnerGuide.title: Time also uses 에
beginnerGuide.body: For clock time, use 에: 7시에 일어나요. Some time words like 오늘, 내일, 지금 usually do not need 에 at beginner level.

checkpoints: I can say where I go with 에.
I can say where I do an action with 에서.
I do not say 학교에서 가요 for destination.

chapters.title: Food And Shopping
chapters.goal: Order items, ask price, pay, and explain simple restrictions.
chapters.scenario: Cafe, restaurant, convenience store, and market.

dialogue.speaker: Staff
dialogue.en: What can I get you?

dialogue.speaker: Learner
dialogue.en: One Americano, please.

dialogue.speaker: Learner
dialogue.en: Bread too, please.

dialogue.speaker: Staff
dialogue.en: Do you need anything else?

dialogue.speaker: Learner
dialogue.en: Only this, please. I'll pay by card.

chapters.guidedPractice: Practice N 주세요, 이것만 주세요, 이것도 주세요, 카드 돼요?, and 카드로 결제할 수 있어요?
chapters.realLifeTask: Order one thing, ask the price, and ask whether card payment is possible.
chapters.friendPractice: Friend plays staff. Learner orders, asks price, and chooses payment.
chapters.review: Can you ask for an item and use 로/으로 for payment?

beginnerGuide.title: Ordering is chunk-based
beginnerGuide.body: In a cafe or store, N 주세요 is more useful than a full English-style sentence. 아메리카노 한 잔 주세요, 빵도 하나 주세요, and 이것만 주세요 are complete practical requests.

beginnerGuide.title: Payment language
beginnerGuide.body: 카드 돼요? is a common spoken shortcut. 카드로 결제할 수 있어요? is clearer and more textbook-complete. Both are useful, but they feel different.

beginnerGuide.title: Small particles, big meaning
beginnerGuide.body: 도 means also, 만 means only, and 로/으로 can show method such as payment or transportation. These small pieces change the shopping situation.

checkpoints: I can order one item with N 주세요.
I can ask price with 얼마예요?
I can ask about card payment using 카드 돼요? or 카드로 결제할 수 있어요?

chapters.title: Want, Can, Cannot
chapters.goal: Talk about desire, ability, possibility, and real limitations.
chapters.scenario: Food choices, schedules, language ability, and travel limits.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.en: What do you want to eat?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.en: I want to eat bibimbap.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.en: Can you go to a cafe today?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.ko: 오늘은 못 가요. 내일 갈 수 있어요.
dialogue.romanization: oneureun mot gayo. naeil gal su isseoyo.
dialogue.en: I can't go today. I can go tomorrow.

chapters.guidedPractice: Transform 가다 into 가고 싶어요, 갈 수 있어요, 못 가요. Transform 먹다 into 먹고 싶어요, 먹을 수 있어요, 못 먹어요.
chapters.realLifeTask: Say what you want to do, what you can do, and what you cannot do.
chapters.friendPractice: Friend asks 갈 수 있어요? Learner answers with 갈 수 있어요 or 못 가요 and a reason.
chapters.review: Can you explain why 못 가해요 is wrong and say 못 가요 instead?

beginnerGuide.title: Three different meanings
beginnerGuide.body: 고 싶어요 is desire, ㄹ/을 수 있어요 is ability or possibility, and 못 + verb is inability. They are not interchangeable.

beginnerGuide.title: The 못 rule beginners need
beginnerGuide.body: For most verbs, put 못 before the normal verb: 못 가요, 못 먹어요. For 하다 verbs, use 못 해요 or noun 못 해요: 공부 못 해요. Do not make 못 가해요.

beginnerGuide.title: Why this chapter matters
beginnerGuide.body: This is the chapter that lets you explain limits politely: I want to go, I can go, I cannot go, I cannot eat spicy food.

checkpoints: I can say want to, can, and cannot with 가다 and 먹다.
I can explain 안 가요 vs 못 가요.
I know 못 가해요 is wrong.

chapters.title: Requests, Permission, And Prohibition
chapters.goal: Ask someone to do something, ask if something is okay, and understand rules.
chapters.scenario: Restaurants, classrooms, museums, stores, and public spaces.

dialogue.speaker: Learner
dialogue.en: Please help me.

dialogue.speaker: Staff
dialogue.en: Sure, how can I help you?

dialogue.speaker: Learner
dialogue.en: May I take a photo?

dialogue.speaker: Staff
dialogue.en: Sorry, but please do not take photos.

chapters.guidedPractice: Practice 도와주세요, 앉아도 돼요?, 가지 마세요, and 가야 해요.
chapters.realLifeTask: Ask for help, ask permission, and understand one prohibition.
chapters.friendPractice: Friend plays staff. Learner asks permission before taking a photo or sitting.
chapters.review: Can you separate request, permission, obligation, and prohibition?

beginnerGuide.title: Requests and permission are different
beginnerGuide.body: V아/어 주세요 asks someone to do something. V아/어도 돼요? asks if you may do something. 사진 찍어 주세요 and 사진 찍어도 돼요? are not the same.

beginnerGuide.title: Prohibition is mostly for understanding first
beginnerGuide.body: 지 마세요 appears on signs and from staff. You can use it, but it can sound like an instruction, so beginners should learn to understand it before using it broadly.

beginnerGuide.title: Make requests softer
beginnerGuide.body: 좀 often softens ordinary requests: 좀 도와주세요, 물 좀 주세요, 잠깐 기다려 주세요.

checkpoints: I can ask for help with 도와주세요.
I can ask permission with 아/어도 돼요?
I can recognize 지 마세요 as “please do not.”

chapters.title: Travel And Classroom Help
chapters.goal: Ask where things are, use transportation, ask for repetition, and explain confusion.
chapters.scenario: Subway station, taxi, hotel, street, airport, or Korean class.

dialogue.speaker: Learner
dialogue.en: Where is the bathroom?

dialogue.speaker: Staff
dialogue.en: It's over there on the right.

dialogue.speaker: Learner
dialogue.en: Sorry, please say it again.

dialogue.speaker: Staff
dialogue.en: Sure. I'll say it slowly. It's over there on the right.

dialogue.speaker: Learner
dialogue.en: I understand. Thank you.

chapters.guidedPractice: Ask where something is, ask someone to repeat, and explain that you do not understand yet.
chapters.realLifeTask: Ask where the bathroom or station is, then ask someone to say it again slowly.
chapters.friendPractice: Friend gives a short direction. Learner asks 다시 말해 주세요 or 천천히 말해 주세요.
chapters.review: Can you ask for location and classroom help without switching to English?

beginnerGuide.title: Travel Korean needs repair phrases
beginnerGuide.body: When communication breaks down, phrases like 다시 말해 주세요, 천천히 말해 주세요, and 잘 모르겠어요 keep the conversation alive.

beginnerGuide.title: Ask short, useful questions
beginnerGuide.body: 화장실 어디예요? and 지하철역 어디예요? are natural spoken questions. Adding 이 makes them more complete, but the shorter form is common.

beginnerGuide.title: Range and route
beginnerGuide.body: 부터/까지 helps with time and route: 여기부터 역까지, 9시부터 6시까지.

checkpoints: I can ask someone to repeat slowly.
I can ask where the bathroom or station is.
I can use 부터/까지 for from-to ranges.

chapters.title: Connecting Ideas
chapters.goal: Move beyond single sentences using because, and, if/when, and speaker promises.
chapters.scenario: Explaining reasons, making plans, and connecting daily actions.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.en: Why can’t you go?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.en: I am busy, so I cannot go.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.en: Can you call later?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.en: Yes, I will call later.

chapters.guidedPractice: Combine two ideas with 아서/어서, then make one promise with ㄹ/을게요.
chapters.realLifeTask: Make one sentence with a reason and one sentence with a condition.
chapters.friendPractice: Friend asks 왜요? Learner answers with one reason sentence.
chapters.review: Can you connect two simple ideas without making a long confusing sentence?

beginnerGuide.title: Longer Korean starts with connectors
beginnerGuide.body: 아서/어서, 고, and 면 let you connect simple sentences. This is how beginner Korean stops sounding like isolated flashcards.

beginnerGuide.title: Reason, sequence, condition
beginnerGuide.body: 아서/어서 gives a reason, 고 connects actions or descriptions, and 면 gives a condition. 바빠서 못 가요, 먹고 가요, 시간이 있으면 전화해 주세요.

beginnerGuide.title: Promise form
beginnerGuide.body: ㄹ/을게요 is for the speaker’s decision or promise: 제가 할게요, 기다릴게요, 전화할게요. Do not use it to predict someone else.

checkpoints: I can connect a reason to a result with 아서/어서.
I can connect two actions with 고.
I can make a simple condition with 면.

chapters.title: Opinions, Reasons & Guessing
chapters.goal: Give opinions, reasons, and soft guesses the way Koreans actually do.
chapters.scenario: Intermediate — build on the beginner chapters.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.en: How was this movie?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.en: Hmm, in my opinion it was a bit boring.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.en: Really? I found it fun, you know.

chapters.title: Society, Culture & Reported Speech
chapters.goal: Talk about society and culture and report what others said.
chapters.scenario: Intermediate — build on the beginner chapters.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.en: Is this an old Korean tradition?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.en: Yes, they say it is a very important tradition.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.en: Even as society changes, traditions remain.

chapters.title: Work, Money & Decisions
chapters.goal: Discuss work and money, and talk about plans and worries.
chapters.scenario: Intermediate — build on the beginner chapters.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.ko: 저 이번에 새 사업을 시작하기로 했어요.
dialogue.romanization: jeo ibeone sae saeobeul sijakhagiro haesseoyo.
dialogue.en: I have decided to start a new business.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.ko: 정말요? 잘 안될까 봐 걱정되진 않아요?
dialogue.romanization: jeongmallyo? jal andoelkka bwa geokjeongdoejin anayo?
dialogue.en: Really? Aren't you worried it might not go well?

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.en: A little. But I am going to give it a try.

chapters.title: Feelings, Personality & Pretending
chapters.goal: Describe deeper feelings and personality, and say what almost happened.
chapters.scenario: Intermediate — build on the beginner chapters.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.en: During the presentation, I pretended to be fine.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.en: It looks like you were really nervous.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.en: Yes. I almost cried.

chapters.title: Connecting Complex Ideas
chapters.goal: Link cause, contrast, and purpose in longer, more natural sentences.
chapters.scenario: Intermediate — build on the beginner chapters.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.en: It was raining, so I practiced at home.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.en: To prepare for the presentation?

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.ko: 네. 연습할수록 더 자연스럽게 말하게 돼요.
dialogue.romanization: ne. yeonseupalsurok deo jayeonseureopge malhage dwaeyo.
dialogue.en: Yes. The more I practice, the more naturally I speak.

chapters.title: Past Tense
chapters.goal: Form polite past tense sentences using 았/었어요 and apply the first irregular verb rules.
chapters.scenario: Telling a friend what you did yesterday.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.en: What did you do yesterday?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.en: I watched a movie with a friend.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.en: The weather was cold, but it was fun.

chapters.guidedPractice: Write five past-tense sentences with 어제, 지난주, or 작년. Include at least one contracted form such as 봤어요, 왔어요, 갔어요, or 했어요.
chapters.realLifeTask: Send or say one short answer to '어제 뭐 했어요?' using a clean past-tense verb.
chapters.friendPractice: A partner gives you a situation; answer with one sentence that uses the chapter's main pattern or vocabulary.
chapters.review: Can you explain why 어제 영화 봐요 is wrong and 어제 영화 봤어요 is right?

beginnerGuide.title: Start with the time word
beginnerGuide.body: When you see 어제, 지난주, or 작년, check that the verb ending is past tense too.

beginnerGuide.title: Memorize the shortcuts
beginnerGuide.body: The forms 했어요, 봤어요, 왔어요, and 갔어요 appear constantly. Learn them as whole spoken chunks.

beginnerGuide.title: First irregular
beginnerGuide.body: 춥다 does not become 춥었어요. It becomes 추웠어요. Treat ㅂ irregular adjectives as a special early warning.

checkpoints: I can answer 어제 뭐 했어요? with one clean past-tense sentence.
I can form 먹었어요, 봤어요, 갔어요, 왔어요, and 했어요.
I can avoid saying 춥었어요 for 추웠어요.

chapters.title: Future and Intention
chapters.goal: Express future plans, intentions, and predictions using -(으)ㄹ 거예요.
chapters.scenario: Making weekend plans with a friend.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.en: What are you going to do this weekend?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.en: I am going to meet a friend and go to a cafe.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.en: If it rains, I am going to study at home.

chapters.guidedPractice: Write five future-plan sentences with 내일, 이번 주말, or 방학. Include both a vowel-stem form like 갈 거예요 and a consonant-stem form like 먹을 거예요.
chapters.realLifeTask: Answer '주말에 뭐 할 거예요?' with one real plan, then add one condition with -면 if useful.
chapters.friendPractice: A partner gives you a situation; answer with one sentence that uses the chapter's main pattern or vocabulary.
chapters.review: Can you explain why 비가 올게요 is wrong and 비가 올 거예요 is right?

beginnerGuide.title: Separate plan and promise
beginnerGuide.body: -(으)ㄹ 거예요 states a plan or prediction. -(으)ㄹ게요 is a promise or offer to the listener.

beginnerGuide.title: Check the stem ending
beginnerGuide.body: Vowel stems take ㄹ 거예요: 갈 거예요, 볼 거예요, 할 거예요. Consonant stems take 을 거예요: 먹을 거예요, 읽을 거예요.

beginnerGuide.title: Use real time words
beginnerGuide.body: Practice with 내일, 이번 주말, 오늘 밤, and 방학 so the future frame is tied to real plans.

checkpoints: I can answer 주말에 뭐 할 거예요? with one real plan.
I can form 갈 거예요, 볼 거예요, 할 거예요, 먹을 거예요, and 읽을 거예요.
I can choose 올 거예요 for weather prediction and 할게요 for my promise.

chapters.title: Question Words
chapters.goal: Use the core Korean question words to ask open-ended follow-up questions.
chapters.scenario: Asking about people, places, times, reasons, and methods in daily conversation.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.en: Where do you learn Korean?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.en: I learn at home through an online class.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.en: When did you start?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.en: I started last year.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.en: Why do you study Korean?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.ko: 한국 친구들과 더 편하게 이야기하고 싶어서요.
dialogue.romanization: hanguk chingudeulgwa deo pyeonhage iyagihago sipeoseoyo.
dialogue.en: Because I want to talk more comfortably with Korean friends.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.en: How do you usually practice?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.en: I watch dramas and repeat the sentences.

chapters.guidedPractice: Write one question each with 뭐, 어디, 언제, 왜, 어떻게, 누구, then answer three of them in Korean.
chapters.realLifeTask: Ask a real follow-up question today: 어디에서요?, 언제부터요?, 왜요?, 어떻게요?, or 누구랑요?
chapters.friendPractice: Partner says 한국어를 배워요. Ask three follow-up questions using different question words, then listen for the answer slot.
chapters.review: Can you explain the difference between 어디에 가요? and 어디에서 공부해요?

beginnerGuide.title: Question words replace answers
beginnerGuide.body: Think from the answer first. 학교에서 공부해요 becomes 어디에서 공부해요? 친구를 만나요 becomes 누구를 만나요?

beginnerGuide.title: Particles still matter
beginnerGuide.body: Use 어디에 for destination or location, 어디에서 for the place where an action happens, 누구를 for the person you meet, and 누구랑 for the person you do something with.

beginnerGuide.title: Do not mix up 어떻게 and 어때요
beginnerGuide.body: 어떻게 asks how to do something: 어떻게 가요? 어때요 asks for an opinion or condition: 영화 어때요?

checkpoints: I can choose the right question word for a thing, place, time, reason, method, or person.
I can use 어디에 and 어디에서 differently.
I can keep the question word in the same slot where the answer would appear.

chapters.title: Numbers and Time
chapters.goal: Use Sino-Korean and native Korean numbers for dates, times, prices, and ages.
chapters.scenario: Arranging to meet at a specific time and discussing prices at a market.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.en: What time shall we meet?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.ko: 세 시 십 분에 지하철역 앞에서 만나요.
dialogue.romanization: se si sip bune jihacheoryeok apeseo mannayo.
dialogue.en: Let's meet at 3:10 in front of the subway station.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.en: How many cups of coffee should we buy?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.ko: 두 잔이면 돼요. 한 잔에 이천오백 원이에요.
dialogue.romanization: du janimyeon dwaeyo. han jane icheonobaek wonieyo.
dialogue.en: Two cups are enough. One cup is 2,500 won.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.en: Then two cups are 5,000 won.

chapters.guidedPractice: Say three clock times, two prices, one date, and one counter phrase aloud: 세 시 십 분, 오천 원, 이월 삼일, 두 잔.
chapters.realLifeTask: Check one real time or price around you and say it in Korean using the correct number family.
chapters.friendPractice: Partner asks 몇 시에 만날까요? and 얼마예요? Learner answers with one time and one price.
chapters.review: Can you explain why 세 시 is right but 삼 분 and 삼천 원 are also right?

beginnerGuide.title: The unit chooses the number family
beginnerGuide.body: Hours and common counters use native numbers: 한 시, 두 잔, 세 명. Minutes, dates, and prices use Sino-Korean numbers: 십 분, 이월 삼일, 오천 원.

beginnerGuide.title: Native numbers change before counters
beginnerGuide.body: 하나, 둘, 셋, 넷 become 한, 두, 세, 네 before counters: 한 시, 두 잔, 세 명, 네 개.

beginnerGuide.title: Age needs politeness
beginnerGuide.body: 나이가 어떻게 되세요? is a safer polite question than 몇 살이에요? with adults or people you do not know well.

checkpoints: I can say clock times with native hours and Sino-Korean minutes.
I can say prices with Sino-Korean numbers and 원.
I can avoid saying 삼 시 when I mean 세 시.

chapters.title: Descriptions
chapters.goal: Describe nouns with adjective and verb modifiers so short sentences become precise phrases.
chapters.scenario: Pointing out the right item in a shop or describing a person you are meeting.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.en: What kind of bag are you looking for?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.ko: 어제 본 작은 가방을 찾고 있어요.
dialogue.romanization: eoje bon jageun gabangeul chatgo isseoyo.
dialogue.en: I am looking for the small bag I saw yesterday.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.en: Here is a new large bag.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.en: Is it a model customers ask for a lot?

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.ko: 네, 출근할 때 들기 좋은 가방이에요.
dialogue.romanization: ne, chulgeunhal ttae deulgi joeun gabangieyo.
dialogue.en: Yes, it is a good bag to carry to work.

chapters.guidedPractice: Build five noun phrases: 예쁜 가방, 작은 지갑, 조용한 카페, 제가 읽는 책, 어제 본 가방.
chapters.realLifeTask: Describe one real item near you with a noun phrase before the noun: 작은 컵, 자주 쓰는 앱, 필요한 물건.
chapters.friendPractice: Partner asks 어떤 가방을 찾으세요? Learner answers with two modifiers before 가방.
chapters.review: Can you explain why 제가 읽는 책 is right but 제가 읽어요 책 is wrong?

beginnerGuide.title: Descriptions go before the noun
beginnerGuide.body: Korean does not say 가방 작은. Put the modifier first: 작은 가방, 예쁜 가방, 제가 읽는 책.

beginnerGuide.title: Adjective or verb decides the ending
beginnerGuide.body: Adjectives use ㄴ/은: 작은 가방, 조용한 카페. Verbs use 는 for present or habitual action: 찾는 모델, 읽는 책.

beginnerGuide.title: Real speech often stacks modifiers
beginnerGuide.body: 어제 본 작은 가방 has two descriptions before one noun: 본 from 보다 and 작은 from 작다.

checkpoints: I can put adjective modifiers before nouns.
I can use V-는 N for present or habitual action descriptions.
I can turn full sentences like 읽어요 into modifiers like 읽는 before a noun.

chapters.title: Likes and Comparisons
chapters.goal: Say what you like and compare choices naturally using 좋아해요, 보다 더, and 만큼.
chapters.scenario: Choosing food, movies, or hobbies with a friend.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.ko: 커피랑 차 중에 뭐가 더 좋아요?
dialogue.romanization: keopirang cha junge mwoga deo joayo?
dialogue.en: Between coffee and tea, which do you like more?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.en: I like coffee more than tea.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.ko: 이 카페 라떼만큼 맛있는 커피가 또 있어요?
dialogue.romanization: i kape rattemankeum masinneun keopiga tto isseoyo?
dialogue.en: Is there another coffee as tasty as this cafe's latte?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.ko: 아직 못 찾았어요. 여기가 제 취향에 제일 맞아요.
dialogue.romanization: ajik mot chajasseoyo. yeogiga je chwihyange jeil majayo.
dialogue.en: I have not found one yet. This place fits my taste the best.

chapters.guidedPractice: Make three preference sentences and two comparisons: 커피를 좋아해요, 차보다 커피를 더 좋아해요, 생각만큼 비싸지 않아요.
chapters.realLifeTask: Choose between two real options today and say why in Korean using 더 좋아해요 or 제 취향에 맞아요.
chapters.friendPractice: Partner asks 커피랑 차 중에 뭐가 더 좋아요? Learner answers with N보다 N을 더 좋아해요 and one reason.
chapters.review: Can you explain why 커피를 좋아해요 and 커피가 좋아요 use different particles?

beginnerGuide.title: 좋아하다 takes 을/를
beginnerGuide.body: Say 커피를 좋아해요 and 음악을 좋아해요. 커피가 좋아해요 is wrong because 좋아하다 is a verb.

beginnerGuide.title: 보다 marks the baseline
beginnerGuide.body: 차보다 커피를 더 좋아해요 means tea is the comparison baseline and coffee is preferred. If you move 보다, the meaning changes.

beginnerGuide.title: 취향 softens preference
beginnerGuide.body: 제 취향이에요 and 제 취향에 맞아요 let you describe personal taste without sounding like the other choice is bad.

checkpoints: I can use 을/를 with 좋아하다 and 싫어하다.
I can attach 보다 to the comparison baseline.
I can use 만큼 for equal-degree comparisons such as 생각만큼 비싸지 않아요.

chapters.title: Directions and Transport
chapters.goal: Use 으로 and 으러 가요 to ask directions and explain transport choices.
chapters.scenario: Finding the subway platform and explaining where you are going.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.en: Which way do I go to get to Hongik University Station?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.en: Go straight on this road and turn right.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.en: Do I go by subway or by bus?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.en: Go by subway. Transfer to Line 2 at City Hall Station.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.ko: 친구 만나러 가는 길이라서 빨리 가야 해요.
dialogue.romanization: chingu mannareo ganeun giriraseo ppalli gaya haeyo.
dialogue.en: I am on my way to meet a friend, so I have to go quickly.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.ko: 그럼 삼 번 출구로 나가서 왼쪽으로 가세요.
dialogue.romanization: geureom sam beon chulguro nagaseo oenjjogeuro gaseyo.
dialogue.en: Then go out through exit three and go left.

chapters.guidedPractice: Make three direction sentences and two purpose sentences: 이 길로 가세요, 지하철로 가요, 친구 만나러 가요.
chapters.realLifeTask: Pick one real destination near you and explain the route in Korean using 로/으로 at least twice.
chapters.friendPractice: Partner asks 어디로 가요? Learner answers with route, transport method, and one purpose using -(으)러.
chapters.review: Can you explain the difference between 지하철역에 가요 and 지하철로 가요?

beginnerGuide.title: 로/으로 is not only 'to'
beginnerGuide.body: It can show direction, route, transport method, or transfer target: 오른쪽으로, 이 길로, 지하철로, 2호선으로.

beginnerGuide.title: 에 still marks destination
beginnerGuide.body: 지하철역에 가요 means go to the subway station. 지하철로 가요 means go by subway. You can combine them: 지하철로 학교에 가요.

beginnerGuide.title: -(으)러 gives the purpose
beginnerGuide.body: 친구 만나러 가요 and 버스 타러 정류장에 가요 explain what you are going to do there.

checkpoints: I can use 로/으로 for direction and transport method.
I can use -(으)러 가요 with a movement verb.
I can ask which exit or direction to use.

chapters.title: Suggestions and Trying
chapters.goal: Make gentle suggestions and invite someone to try an action before deciding.
chapters.scenario: Suggesting a restaurant, trying on clothes, or asking for help politely.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.en: Should I try this clothing on once?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.en: Yes, try it on. It suits you well.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.en: Then please recommend another color too.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.en: Try on this color too.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.ko: 사이즈가 크면 한 치수 작은 것도 보여 주세요.
dialogue.romanization: saijeuga keumyeon han chisu jageun geotdo boyeo juseyo.
dialogue.en: If the size is big, please show me one size smaller too.

chapters.guidedPractice: Make two trying sentences, two polite requests, and one suggestion: 입어 보세요, 추천해 주세요, 같이 갈까요?
chapters.realLifeTask: Choose one real item, food, or app and say a low-pressure suggestion with 한번 -아/어 보세요.
chapters.friendPractice: Partner asks 이 옷 어때요? Learner answers with 입어 보세요, 추천해 주세요, or 보여 주세요.
chapters.review: Can you explain why 입어 보세요 is softer than 입으세요?

beginnerGuide.title: Trying lowers pressure
beginnerGuide.body: 입어 보세요 means try it on before deciding. 한번 makes the suggestion even lighter: 한번 입어 보세요.

beginnerGuide.title: 주세요 makes requests polite
beginnerGuide.body: Use 추천해 주세요, 보여 주세요, 바꿔 주세요, and 도와주세요 when asking someone to do something for you.

beginnerGuide.title: ㄹ까요 checks the decision
beginnerGuide.body: 갈까요? can mean shall we go or should I go. 입어 볼까요? asks whether trying it on is a good idea.

checkpoints: I can use -아/어 보다 for trying an action.
I can use -아/어 주세요 for polite requests.
I can use ㄹ/을까요? to suggest or ask what to do.

chapters.title: Contrast and Concession
chapters.goal: Connect ideas with but/even though nuance instead of listing everything with 그리고.
chapters.scenario: Explaining a plan that is good but expensive, or continuing despite a problem.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.en: This restaurant is expensive, but it is really delicious.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.en: But there are too many people today.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.en: Even if there are many people, the food comes out quickly.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.en: Even though it is raining, there are many people waiting.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.en: Still, shall we give it a try?

chapters.guidedPractice: Make three pairs: 비싸지만 맛있어요, 비싸도 갈 거예요, 비싼데도 사람이 많아요. Say what changes in the feeling each time.
chapters.realLifeTask: Write one real plan with a drawback: 시간이 없지만 갈 거예요, 비가 와도 갈 거예요, or 비가 오는데도 사람이 많아요.
chapters.friendPractice: One person gives an obstacle such as 비싸요, 어려워요, 피곤해요. The other answers with -지만, -아/어도, or -는데도 and explains the choice.
chapters.review: Can you separate simple contrast (-지만), condition that does not change the result (-아/어도), and surprising result (-는데도)?

beginnerGuide.title: Three kinds of but
beginnerGuide.body: -지만 is the plain contrast form: 비싸지만 맛있어요. Use it when two facts pull in different directions without extra emotion.

beginnerGuide.title: Even if the plan stays
beginnerGuide.body: -아/어도 says the result does not change: 비가 와도 갈 거예요, 어려워도 해 볼게요. 괜찮아요 and 상관없어요 pair naturally with this form.

beginnerGuide.title: Even though it is surprising
beginnerGuide.body: -는데도 reacts to an actual situation where the expected result did not happen: 비가 오는데도 사람이 많아요. It sounds stronger than plain -지만.

checkpoints: I can use -지만 for a simple contrast.
I can use -아/어도 when the result stays the same despite a condition.
I can use -는데도 when the result feels surprising or frustrating.

chapters.title: Probability and Inference
chapters.goal: Make softened guesses and evidence-based inferences without sounding too certain.
chapters.scenario: Guessing why someone is late or whether it will rain.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.ko: 하늘이 갑자기 흐려졌어요. 곧 비가 올 것 같아요.
dialogue.romanization: haneuri gapjagi heuryeojyeosseoyo. got biga ol geot gatayo.
dialogue.en: The sky suddenly got cloudy. I think it will rain soon.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.ko: 사람들이 우산을 꺼내네요. 벌써 비가 조금 오나 봐요.
dialogue.romanization: saramdeuri usaneul kkeonaeneyo. beolsseo biga jogeum ona bwayo.
dialogue.en: People are taking out umbrellas. I guess it is already raining a little.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.ko: 수진 씨 답장도 없어요. 많이 바쁜가 봐요.
dialogue.romanization: sujin ssi dapjangdo eopseoyo. mani bappeunga bwayo.
dialogue.en: Su-jin is not replying either. I guess she is really busy.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.en: If the bus is stuck too, she might be a little late.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.en: Since we are not sure, let's wait inside the cafe.

chapters.guidedPractice: Build three guesses from clues: 하늘이 흐려요 -> 비가 올 것 같아요; 우산을 꺼내요 -> 비가 오나 봐요; 버스가 막혀요 -> 늦을지도 몰라요.
chapters.realLifeTask: Send one real soft update such as 조금 늦을 것 같아요, 답장이 없어서 바쁜가 봐요, or 비가 올지도 몰라요.
chapters.friendPractice: One person gives a clue. The other chooses 것 같아요, 나 봐요, or ㄹ지도 몰라요 and explains how certain the guess feels.
chapters.review: Can you tell the difference between a soft prediction, an evidence-based inference, and an open possibility?

beginnerGuide.title: Soft prediction
beginnerGuide.body: Use -(으)ㄹ 것 같아요 when you have an impression but not a fact: 비가 올 것 같아요, 조금 늦을 것 같아요.

beginnerGuide.title: Guess from a clue
beginnerGuide.body: Use -나 봐요 or -(으)ㄴ가 봐요 when something you see or hear supports the guess: 우산을 꺼내네요. 비가 오나 봐요.

beginnerGuide.title: Possible, not certain
beginnerGuide.body: Use -(으)ㄹ지도 몰라요 when you want to warn that something might happen: 버스가 늦을지도 몰라요.

checkpoints: I can use -(으)ㄹ 것 같아요 for a soft prediction.
I can use -나 봐요 or -(으)ㄴ가 봐요 when there is a clue.
I can use -(으)ㄹ지도 몰라요 for an open possibility.

chapters.title: Ongoing Actions
chapters.goal: Describe actions in progress using -고 있다, -는 중이에요, and duration frames.
chapters.scenario: Texting someone what you are doing right now.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.en: What are you doing now?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.en: I am studying Korean at the library.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.en: I am waiting for a friend.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.ko: 아까 회의하는 동안 메시지를 못 봤어요.
dialogue.romanization: akka hoeuihaneun dongan mesijireul mot bwasseoyo.
dialogue.en: Earlier, I could not see the message during the meeting.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.en: It is okay. Please call for a moment when you finish.

chapters.guidedPractice: Make one status sentence with each frame: 공부하고 있어요, 기다리는 중이에요, 회의하는 동안 메시지를 못 봤어요.
chapters.realLifeTask: Send or draft one real status reply: 지금 일하는 중이에요, 잠깐 쉬고 있어요, or 회의 중이라 나중에 전화할게요.
chapters.friendPractice: One person asks 지금 뭐 하고 있어요? The other answers once with -고 있어요, once with -는 중이에요, and once with -는 동안.
chapters.review: Can you choose between broad ongoing action, in-the-middle status, and overlapping duration?

beginnerGuide.title: Action in progress
beginnerGuide.body: Use -고 있어요 for an action happening now or around now: 공부하고 있어요, 전화하고 있어요, 쉬고 있어요.

beginnerGuide.title: In the middle
beginnerGuide.body: Use -는 중이에요 or N 중이에요 for a quick current-status reply: 기다리는 중이에요, 회의 중이에요, 전화 중이에요.

beginnerGuide.title: During the span
beginnerGuide.body: Use -는 동안 when another action happens inside the same time span: 회의하는 동안 메시지를 못 봤어요.

checkpoints: I can use -고 있어요 for an action in progress.
I can use -는 중이에요 or N 중이에요 for current status.
I can use -는 동안 for overlapping time.

chapters.title: Sequence and Completion
chapters.goal: Order events with after/as soon as language and mark completed actions clearly.
chapters.scenario: Explaining your morning routine or travel steps.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.en: What order did you get ready in this morning?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.ko: 먼저 손을 씻고 나서 아침을 먹었어요.
dialogue.romanization: meonjeo soneul ssitgo naseo achimeul meogeosseoyo.
dialogue.en: First, after washing my hands, I ate breakfast.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.en: Then did you leave right away?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.ko: 네, 그런데 집에서 나오자마자 지갑을 두고 온 걸 알았어요.
dialogue.romanization: ne, geureonde jibeseo naojamaja jigabeul dugo on geol arasseoyo.
dialogue.en: Yes, but as soon as I came out of the house, I realized I had left my wallet behind.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.en: So did you go back up?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.ko: 네, 지갑을 챙기고 나서 다시 출발했어요.
dialogue.romanization: ne, jigabeul chaenggigo naseo dasi chulbalhaesseoyo.
dialogue.en: Yes, after grabbing my wallet, I left again.

chapters.guidedPractice: Explain a morning routine with 먼저, 그다음, -고 나서, and -자마자: 손을 씻고 나서 먹었어요; 나오자마자 지갑을 두고 온 걸 알았어요.
chapters.realLifeTask: Write one real sequence update: 도착하자마자 전화할게요, 준비하고 나서 출발했어요, or 예약을 확인하고 나서 올라갔어요.
chapters.friendPractice: One person asks what happened first and next. The other answers with one -고 나서 sentence and one -자마자 sentence.
chapters.review: Can you separate completed sequence (-고 나서) from immediate sequence (-자마자)?

beginnerGuide.title: Completed first
beginnerGuide.body: Use -고 나서 when the first action is finished before the next one starts: 손을 씻고 나서 밥을 먹어요.

beginnerGuide.title: No gap
beginnerGuide.body: Use -자마자 when the second action happens immediately: 도착하자마자 전화해 주세요.

beginnerGuide.title: Timeline words
beginnerGuide.body: 먼저, 그다음, 바로, 방금, and 이미 make the order and completion status clear.

checkpoints: I can use -고 나서 for an action completed before the next step.
I can use -자마자 for an immediate next action.
I can avoid putting tense before -자마자 or -고 나서.

chapters.title: Mid-Action Change
chapters.goal: Use -다가 and result-state forms to explain interruption, switching, and changed situations.
chapters.scenario: A plan changes while you are on the way or in the middle of doing something.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.ko: 학교에 가다가 수업 취소 문자를 받았어요.
dialogue.romanization: hakgyoe gadaga sueop chwiso munjareul badasseoyo.
dialogue.en: I got a class cancellation text while I was on my way to school.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.ko: 지하철을 타고 있다가 수업 취소 문자를 받았어요?
dialogue.romanization: jihacheoreul tago itdaga sueop chwiso munjareul badasseoyo?
dialogue.en: Did you get a class cancellation text while riding the subway?

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.en: Yes, so I changed the plan midway.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.en: Where are you now?

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.ko: 카페에 앉아 있어요. 문도 열려 있고 불도 켜져 있어요.
dialogue.romanization: kapee anja isseoyo. mundo yeollyeo itgo buldo kyeojyeo isseoyo.
dialogue.en: I am sitting at a cafe. The door is open and the light is on.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.en: Then rest a little and go again.

chapters.guidedPractice: Make three -다가 sentences and two result-state sentences: 학교에 가다가 전화를 받았어요; 카페에 앉아 있어요; 문이 열려 있어요.
chapters.realLifeTask: Write one real changed-plan message: 가다가 문자를 받았어요, 중간에 계획을 바꿨어요, or 조금 쉬다가 다시 갈 거예요.
chapters.friendPractice: One person gives an interrupted action. The other answers with -다가, then describes the new state with -아/어 있어요.
chapters.review: Can you tell when the first action was interrupted (-다가) and when a result state remains (-아/어 있다)?

beginnerGuide.title: Interrupted action
beginnerGuide.body: Use -다가 when the first action is underway and then something changes: 학교에 가다가 전화를 받았어요.

beginnerGuide.title: Changed plan words
beginnerGuide.body: 중간에, 계획, 바꾸다, 취소하다, 문자, and 갑자기 help explain why the original action changed.

beginnerGuide.title: Result state
beginnerGuide.body: Use -아/어 있어요 for the state that remains: 앉아 있어요, 문이 열려 있어요, 불이 켜져 있어요.

checkpoints: I can use -다가 for an interrupted or changed action.
I can use -아/어 있어요 for a continuing result state.
I can avoid using -다가 when the first action fully finished.

chapters.title: Cause and Unexpected Result
chapters.goal: Explain ordinary causes and unexpected bad outcomes with the right connector.
chapters.scenario: Explaining why you were late or why a plan got canceled.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.en: Why was the appointment canceled?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.ko: 갑자기 비가 많이 오는 바람에 길이 막혔어요.
dialogue.romanization: gapjagi biga mani oneun barame giri makhyeosseoyo.
dialogue.en: It suddenly rained a lot, so the roads got jammed.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.en: Because of the rain, you could not take a taxi either?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.ko: 네. 버스까지 고장 나는 바람에 다들 늦었어요.
dialogue.romanization: ne. beoseukkaji gojang naneun barame dadeul neujeosseoyo.
dialogue.en: Right. Even the bus broke down, so everyone was late.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.en: So you moved the gathering to next week.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.en: Yes. I said I was sorry for being late.

chapters.guidedPractice: Make one sentence with each cause shape: 길이 막혀서 늦었어요, 버스가 고장 나는 바람에 늦었어요, 비 때문에 취소했어요. Then change the cause word.
chapters.realLifeTask: Draft one polite message explaining why you are late or why a plan changed, and add a short apology if the other person was inconvenienced.
chapters.friendPractice: A partner asks 왜 늦었어요? or 왜 취소됐어요? Answer once with -아서/어서, once with -는 바람에, and once with N 때문에.
chapters.review: Can you choose between neutral cause, unexpected-disruption cause, and noun cause without saying 비가 때문에?

beginnerGuide.title: Three cause shapes
beginnerGuide.body: Use -아서/어서 for ordinary reason-result, -는 바람에 for an unexpected event that caused trouble, and N 때문에 when the cause is a noun.

beginnerGuide.title: Use real situation words
beginnerGuide.body: 비, 길, 버스, 택시, 약속, 모임, 막히다, 고장나다, 놓치다, 늦다, and 취소하다 all belong to the same late-or-canceled-plan scene.

beginnerGuide.title: Watch the tone
beginnerGuide.body: 바람에 can sound like an excuse because it points to something that disrupted the plan. If someone waited for you, add 죄송해요 or 미안해요.

checkpoints: I can choose -아서/어서, -는 바람에, or N 때문에 based on the cause.
I can say 비 때문에, not 비가 때문에.
I can explain a late arrival or canceled plan with real linked words from this chapter.

chapters.title: Purpose and Duration
chapters.goal: Explain why you do something and how long it lasts.
chapters.scenario: Telling someone why you came to Korea and how long you will stay.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.en: Why did you come to Korea?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.ko: 한국어를 배우기 위해서 왔어요. 세 달 동안 머물 거예요.
dialogue.romanization: hangugeoreul baeugi wihaeseo wasseoyo. se dal dongan meomul geoyeyo.
dialogue.en: I came in order to learn Korean. I will stay for three months.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.ko: 한국에 있는 동안 뭐 할 거예요?
dialogue.romanization: hanguge inneun dongan mwo hal geoyeyo?
dialogue.en: What will you do while you are in Korea?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.ko: 취업을 위해서 매일 한국어를 연습할 거예요.
dialogue.romanization: chwieobeul wihaeseo maeil hangugeoreul yeonseupal geoyeyo.
dialogue.en: I will practice Korean every day in order to get a job.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.en: Are you preparing for an exam too?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.ko: 네, 합격하기 위해서 방학 동안 계속 공부할 거예요.
dialogue.romanization: ne, hapgyeokagi wihaeseo banghak dongan gyesok gongbuhal geoyeyo.
dialogue.en: Yes, I will keep studying during vacation in order to pass.

chapters.guidedPractice: Make two purpose sentences and two duration sentences: 배우기 위해서 왔어요, 취업을 위해서 연습해요, 세 달 동안 머물 거예요, 한국에 있는 동안 공부할 거예요.
chapters.realLifeTask: Write a short self-introduction explaining one goal and one time span: why you are studying and how long you plan to keep it up.
chapters.friendPractice: A partner asks 왜 왔어요? and 얼마 동안 있을 거예요? Answer with -기 위해서, N을/를 위해서, N 동안, and V-는 동안.
chapters.review: Can you keep purpose 'for' and duration 'for' separate in Korean?

beginnerGuide.title: Two kinds of for
beginnerGuide.body: English uses 'for' in 취업을 위해서 and 세 달 동안, but Korean separates purpose from duration. 위해서 gives the goal; 동안 gives the time span.

beginnerGuide.title: Purpose needs the right shape
beginnerGuide.body: Use V-기 위해서 for verb goals like 배우기 위해서 and 합격하기 위해서. Use N을/를 위해서 for noun goals like 취업을 위해서 and 건강을 위해서.

beginnerGuide.title: Duration is a span
beginnerGuide.body: Use 세 달 동안, 방학 동안, and 한국에 있는 동안 to show the time period. Do not say 세 달에 동안 or 방학에 동안.

checkpoints: I can use V-기 위해서 and N을/를 위해서 for goals.
I can use N 동안 and V-는 동안 for time spans.
I can avoid confusing purpose 'for' with duration 'for'.

chapters.title: Decisions and Changes
chapters.goal: Describe decisions, life changes, and state changes using 기로 했어요, 게 되다, and 아/어지다.
chapters.scenario: Explaining a new habit, a changed schedule, or a decision you made.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.en: What will be different starting next month?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.en: I decided to exercise every morning.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.en: Did you decide that yourself?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.ko: 네, 건강이 안 좋아져서 시작하기로 했어요.
dialogue.romanization: ne, geongangi an joajyeoseo sijakagiro haesseoyo.
dialogue.en: Yes, my health got worse, so I decided to start.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.en: Have your habits already changed?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.ko: 네. 일찍 자게 되고 몸도 가벼워졌어요.
dialogue.romanization: ne. iljjik jage doego momdo gabyeowojyeosseoyo.
dialogue.en: Yes. I came to sleep earlier, and my body feels lighter too.

chapters.guidedPractice: Make one sentence for each change type: 운동하기로 했어요, 일찍 자게 됐어요, 건강이 좋아졌어요. Then change the verb or state.
chapters.realLifeTask: Write a short update about one decision you made and one change you can feel now.
chapters.friendPractice: A partner asks 뭐가 달라졌어요? Answer with -기로 했어요, -게 됐어요, and -아/어졌어요.
chapters.review: Can you tell the difference between a decision, a situation you ended up in, and a changed state?

beginnerGuide.title: Agency comes first
beginnerGuide.body: Use -기로 했어요 when you made the decision. Use -게 됐어요 when circumstances led to the result. Use -아/어졌어요 when the state itself changed.

beginnerGuide.title: Use change words together
beginnerGuide.body: 결정하다, 시작하다, 바뀌다, 달라지다, 좋아지다, 늘다, and 줄다 help explain what changed in a real routine or study plan.

beginnerGuide.title: Do not hide decisions
beginnerGuide.body: If you simply chose something, say 운동하기로 했어요. Use 운동하게 됐어요 only when the situation led you there.

checkpoints: I can use -기로 했어요 for a settled decision.
I can use -게 됐어요 for a situation that came about.
I can use -아/어졌어요 for a changed state like 좋아졌어요 or 가벼워졌어요.

chapters.title: Speech Levels
chapters.goal: Switch between 해요체 and formal 합쇼체 based on setting and relationship.
chapters.scenario: Giving a short presentation and then speaking casually with a classmate afterward.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.en: What speech style should I use in a presentation?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.en: Since it is a formal setting, start in formal polite style.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.en: Then what do I say at the beginning?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.en: It sounds natural to say, “I will begin the presentation now.”

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.en: Do I speak like that to a friend afterward too?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.ko: 아니요. 친구에게는 해요체로 “발표 끝났어요” 정도가 좋아요.
dialogue.romanization: aniyo. chinguegeneun haeyochero balpyo kkeunnasseoyo jeongdoga joayo.
dialogue.en: No. With a friend, haeyo style like “The presentation is over” is good.

chapters.guidedPractice: Make one formal presentation sentence and one classmate sentence: 발표를 시작하겠습니다, 발표 끝났어요. Then explain why the speech level changes.
chapters.realLifeTask: Rewrite one sentence in two styles: 합쇼체 for a presentation or interview, and 해요체 for a classmate or teacher after class.
chapters.friendPractice: A partner gives you a setting: 발표, 면접, 선생님, 친구, or 처음 만난 사람. Choose 해요체, 합쇼체, 존댓말, or 반말 and say why.
chapters.review: Can you choose a speech level from relationship and setting, not just from English politeness?

beginnerGuide.title: Setting changes the ending
beginnerGuide.body: Use 합쇼체 in formal public settings like 발표 and 면접. Use 해요체 for ordinary polite conversation with classmates, teachers, and people you just met.

beginnerGuide.title: Polite is not one style
beginnerGuide.body: 존댓말 is the broad polite category. 해요체 and 합쇼체 are both polite, but 합쇼체 sounds more formal and public.

beginnerGuide.title: Use 반말 carefully
beginnerGuide.body: 반말 is natural with close friends, but it can sound rude with teachers, staff, strangers, or people who have not agreed to speak casually.

checkpoints: I can use -습니다/ㅂ니다 and -습니까 for formal polite speech.
I can explain when 해요체 sounds better than 합쇼체.
I can avoid using 반말 before the relationship allows it.

chapters.title: Honorifics
chapters.goal: Honor the sentence subject using -(으)시- and respectful particles without overusing them.
chapters.scenario: Talking about a teacher, parent, or customer respectfully.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.en: When is the teacher coming?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.en: They will come soon and speak first.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.en: Did you contact your parents too?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.en: Yes, I told my mother first.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.en: Is the boss here now?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.en: Yes, they are in the meeting room.

chapters.guidedPractice: Make one subject-honor sentence and one recipient-honor sentence: 선생님께서 오세요, 선생님께 말씀드렸어요. Then explain the difference.
chapters.realLifeTask: Write a respectful message or note about a teacher, parent, boss, or customer using 께서 or 께 correctly.
chapters.friendPractice: A partner gives you a person and an action. Decide whether the person is the subject or recipient, then choose 께서, 께, -(으)시-, or 드리다.
chapters.review: Can you tell who receives the respect before choosing the honorific form?

beginnerGuide.title: Respect has direction
beginnerGuide.body: -(으)시- and 께서 honor the subject. 께 and 드리다 honor the person who receives your action.

beginnerGuide.title: Use special verbs
beginnerGuide.body: 계시다, 드시다, 주무시다, and 말씀하시다 are not random alternatives; they are common honorific verbs for respected subjects.

beginnerGuide.title: Do not honor yourself
beginnerGuide.body: Do not add -(으)시- to your own action. Say 제가 가요, not 제가 가세요. Use 드리다 only when your action goes toward someone respected.

checkpoints: I can use -(으)시- and 께서 for a respected subject.
I can use 께 and 드리다 for a respected recipient.
I can avoid using honorifics on myself or on objects.

chapters.title: Discourse Markers
chapters.goal: Use Korean softeners and background endings to bring up a topic, give context, and disagree without sounding abrupt.
chapters.scenario: A study or work meeting where materials are late and the speaker needs to explain the background carefully.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.ko: 사실은 오늘 자료가 아직 다 안 끝났는데요.
dialogue.romanization: sasireun oneul jaryoga ajik da an kkeunnanneundeyo.
dialogue.en: Actually, today's materials are not finished yet.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.ko: 그러니까 먼저 회의를 시작해도 된다는 말이죠?
dialogue.romanization: geureonikka meonjeo hoeuireul sijakaedo doendaneun marijyo?
dialogue.en: So you mean we can start the meeting first, right?

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.en: Yes. Something suddenly came up yesterday, you see.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.ko: 알겠어요. 그런데 발표 전에 자료는 보내 줄 수 있어요?
dialogue.romanization: algesseoyo. geureonde balpyo jeone jaryoneun bonae jul su isseoyo?
dialogue.en: I understand. But can you send the materials before the presentation?

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.ko: 네, 그건 가능해요. 회의 시간이 짧잖아요.
dialogue.romanization: ne, geugeon ganeunghaeyo. hoeui sigani jjaljanhayo.
dialogue.en: Yes, that is possible. The meeting time is short, you know.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.en: Then I will explain the background first.

chapters.guidedPractice: Make three meeting-message lines: one with 사실은 ...는데요, one with ...거든요 for new background, and one with ...잖아요 for shared information.
chapters.realLifeTask: Write a short message about a late file, changed plan, or soft disagreement using 사실은, 그런데, and one of -는데요, -거든요, or -잖아요.
chapters.friendPractice: One person gives a problem in a meeting or study group. The other brings it up softly, then explains whether the reason is new information or shared information.
chapters.review: Can you choose 거든요 for new background and 잖아요 for shared information without making the listener feel blamed?

beginnerGuide.title: Open the topic softly
beginnerGuide.body: 사실은 and -는데요 let you start a sensitive topic without sounding like you are dropping bad news too suddenly.

beginnerGuide.title: Separate new and shared information
beginnerGuide.body: Use -거든요 when the listener does not know the background yet. Use -잖아요 when the listener already knows or can see the reason.

beginnerGuide.title: Soften disagreement
beginnerGuide.body: 그런데, 근데, and -는데요 can make pushback feel conversational, but the sentence still needs a clear point.

checkpoints: I can bring up late materials or a changed plan with 사실은 ...는데요.
I can use -거든요 for new background and -잖아요 for shared information.
I can soften disagreement with 그런데 or -는데요 without hiding the main point.

chapters.title: Observation and Retrospection
chapters.goal: Report what you personally noticed and how a situation changed over time.
chapters.scenario: Telling a friend what you personally noticed after visiting a restaurant or event.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.ko: 어제 새 식당에 가 보니까 어땠어요?
dialogue.romanization: eoje sae sikdange ga bonikka eottaesseoyo?
dialogue.en: How was it when you tried going to the new restaurant yesterday?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.en: It was quiet at first, and then it quickly got crowded, I noticed.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.en: How was the food?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.en: It came out faster than expected, and the taste was good too.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.en: I heard there used to be fewer people.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.en: Right. These days, the atmosphere has changed a lot, I noticed.

chapters.guidedPractice: Describe one place you visited with 가 보니까 ...더라고요, then add one change sentence with 처음에는 ...더니 ...졌어요.
chapters.realLifeTask: Send or draft a short review of a restaurant, cafe, class, or event using 생각보다 and -더라고요.
chapters.friendPractice: One person asks about a place or event. The other gives one firsthand observation and one observed change over time.
chapters.review: Can you tell the difference between a plain past fact and a firsthand observation with -더라고요?

beginnerGuide.title: Firsthand evidence
beginnerGuide.body: -더라고요 means you saw, tried, felt, or realized something yourself. It is not for information you only heard from someone else.

beginnerGuide.title: Observed change
beginnerGuide.body: -더니 links an earlier thing you observed to the change or result that followed: 처음에는 조용하더니 금방 붐볐어요.

beginnerGuide.title: Your own result
beginnerGuide.body: For your own action causing a result, use -았/었더니: 많이 먹었더니 졸렸어요. Plain -더니 usually watches someone or something else change.

checkpoints: I can use -더라고요 to report what I personally noticed.
I can use -더니 to connect an observed earlier state/action to a later change.
I can avoid using plain -더니 for my own neutral action when -았/었더니 is needed.

chapters.title: Reported Speech
chapters.goal: Report statements, questions, and embedded questions accurately.
chapters.scenario: Passing along a teacher's instructions and a friend's questions after class.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.en: What did the teacher say?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.en: The teacher told us to submit the homework by tomorrow.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.en: Did the teacher also say when the exam is?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.en: Yes, the teacher said we will take it on Friday.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.en: What did your friend ask?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.en: They asked what time we are meeting.

chapters.guidedPractice: Report three things from class: one statement with -다고 했어요, one question with -냐고 물어봤어요, and one embedded question with -는지.
chapters.realLifeTask: Draft a message to a classmate passing along homework, exam time, or meeting details using one reported-speech form.
chapters.friendPractice: One person plays the teacher or friend and says a statement, question, or instruction. The other reports it accurately.
chapters.review: Can you match the reported ending to the original sentence type: statement, question, or instruction?

beginnerGuide.title: Match the source sentence
beginnerGuide.body: Statements use -다고 했어요, questions use -냐고 물어봤어요, and instructions use -(으)라고 했어요.

beginnerGuide.title: Embed questions with -는지
beginnerGuide.body: Use -는지 when the question becomes part of another sentence: 시험이 언제인지 알아요?, 몇 시에 만나는지 확인해 주세요.

beginnerGuide.title: Do not translate English word order
beginnerGuide.body: English uses 'said that' and 'asked if,' but Korean changes the inner ending. The ending shows whether the original was a statement or a question.

checkpoints: I can report a statement with -다고 했어요 or the spoken contraction -대요.
I can report a question with -냐고 물어봤어요.
I can use -는지 with 알다, 모르다, 확인하다, or 궁금하다.

chapters.title: Advanced Noun Modification and Passive
chapters.goal: Build longer noun phrases and recognize passive or causative verb forms in real sentences.
chapters.scenario: Reading a school or work notice where schedule changes and result-focused passive forms are compressed into noun phrases.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.en: Did you see the notice posted yesterday?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.ko: 네, 발표 시간이 다음 주로 잡혔어요.
dialogue.romanization: ne, balpyo sigani daeum juro japyeosseoyo.
dialogue.en: Yes, the presentation time was set for next week.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.ko: 변경된 일정이 표 아래에 작게 쓰여 있었어요.
dialogue.romanization: byeongyeongdoen iljeongi pyo araee jakge sseuyeo isseosseoyo.
dialogue.en: The changed schedule was written in small print below the table.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.ko: 저는 그 문장이 처음에 잘 안 읽혔어요.
dialogue.romanization: jeoneun geu munjangi cheoeume jal an ilkhyeosseoyo.
dialogue.en: At first, that sentence did not read clearly to me.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.ko: 담당자가 학생들을 앞자리에 앉힌다는 내용도 있었어요.
dialogue.romanization: damdangjaga haksaengdeureul apjarie anjhindaneun naeyongdo isseosseoyo.
dialogue.en: It also said the staff would seat students in the front rows.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.ko: 그러니까 누가 바꿨는지보다 뭐가 바뀌었는지가 중요하네요.
dialogue.romanization: geureonikka nuga bakkwonneunjiboda mwoga bakkwieonneunjiga jungyohaneyo.
dialogue.en: So what changed matters more than who changed it.

chapters.guidedPractice: Take one long notice sentence and underline the final noun first: 공지, 일정, 문장, 내용, or 보고서. Then unpack the phrase before it.
chapters.realLifeTask: Find one real notice, product page, or article sentence and identify one compressed noun phrase plus one passive/result-focused verb.
chapters.friendPractice: One person gives a short notice sentence. The other says the final noun first, then explains what modifier or passive verb describes it.
chapters.review: Can you read 변경된 일정 or 어제 올라온 공지 as one noun phrase instead of separate beginner sentences?

beginnerGuide.title: Find the final noun
beginnerGuide.body: In long Korean noun phrases, the important noun comes at the end: 올라온 공지, 변경된 일정, 제출할 보고서.

beginnerGuide.title: Passive focuses the result
beginnerGuide.body: 잡히다, 닫히다, 팔리다, and 보이다 make the schedule, door, product, or visible thing the subject.

beginnerGuide.title: Causative adds a controller
beginnerGuide.body: 먹이다, 앉히다, and 입히다 add someone who causes another person to eat, sit, or wear something.

checkpoints: I can unpack noun phrases like 어제 올라온 공지 and 변경된 일정.
I can recognize passive/result verbs like 잡히다, 닫히다, 팔리다, and 보이다.
I can separate passive result focus from causative control forms like 먹이다, 앉히다, and 입히다.

chapters.title: Inevitability and Limits
chapters.goal: Express no-choice situations, impossibility, and “only” nuance without sounding flat.
chapters.scenario: Explaining a deadline situation where the team has no choice, refuses to give up, and has only one workable method left.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.en: The deadline is today, so we have no choice but to work late.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.en: Still, there is no way we would give up now.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.ko: 자료는 맞지만 설명은 다시 쓸 수밖에 없어요.
dialogue.romanization: jaryoneun matjiman seolmyeongeun dasi sseul subakke eopseoyo.
dialogue.en: The data is right, but we have no choice but to rewrite the explanation.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.en: In the end, this method is the only thing left.

chapters.guidedPractice: Write one deadline sentence with -ㄹ 수밖에 없다, one strong denial with -ㄹ 리가 없다, and one only-option sentence with -뿐이다.
chapters.realLifeTask: Draft a short team-project message explaining a no-choice deadline situation without using English-style 'I cannot do it' for 'I have no choice.'
chapters.friendPractice: One person gives a constraint such as 마감, 규칙, 품절, or 시간이 부족하다. The other explains the only option and rejects one impossible misunderstanding.
chapters.review: Can you separate no choice (-ㄹ 수밖에 없다), strong impossibility (-ㄹ 리가 없다), and only/nothing more (-뿐이다)?

beginnerGuide.title: No choice is not cannot
beginnerGuide.body: 할 수 없어요 means you cannot do it. 할 수밖에 없어요 means you must do it because there is no other option.

beginnerGuide.title: 리가 없다 is strong disbelief
beginnerGuide.body: 포기할 리가 없어요 means the speaker strongly rejects that possibility. It is stronger than 아마 포기하지 않을 거예요.

beginnerGuide.title: 뿐이다 closes the scope
beginnerGuide.body: 이 방법뿐이에요 means only this method remains. It differs from 뿐만 아니라, which adds another point.

checkpoints: I can use -ㄹ 수밖에 없다 for no-choice situations without confusing it with -ㄹ 수 없다.
I can use -ㄹ 리가 없다 to strongly reject a possibility.
I can use -뿐이다 to show that only one action, role, or method remains.

chapters.title: Nuance and Hedging
chapters.goal: Add nuance to guesses, wishes, hypotheticals, and careful opinions.
chapters.scenario: Giving a careful opinion without sounding too blunt or overconfident.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.en: They are probably still in a meeting.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.en: Hmm, they may have already left work.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.ko: 혹시 이미 나갔다면 메시지를 남겨 두면 좋겠어요.
dialogue.romanization: hoksi imi nagatdamyeon mesijireul namgyeo dumyeon jokesseoyo.
dialogue.en: If they already left, it would be good to leave a message.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.en: Since I am not sure, I will ask carefully.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.ko: 제 생각에는 먼저 물어보는 게 좋을 것 같아요.
dialogue.romanization: je saenggageneun meonjeo mureoboneun ge joeul geot gatayo.
dialogue.en: In my opinion, I think it would be good to ask first.

chapters.guidedPractice: Turn three blunt statements into careful Korean: one with -ㄹ걸요, one with -다면, and one with -는 것 같아요.
chapters.realLifeTask: Send or draft a careful message about an uncertain situation, using 글쎄요, 혹시, or 제 생각에는 plus one hedge from this chapter.
chapters.friendPractice: A partner gives you an uncertain workplace or group-chat situation; answer with a guess, a hypothetical, and a gentle suggestion.
chapters.review: Can you choose between -ㄹ걸요, -다면, -겠-, 좋겠어요, and 것 같아요 instead of using one vague 'I think' for everything?

beginnerGuide.title: Guess without overclaiming
beginnerGuide.body: -ㄹ걸요 gives a soft but fairly confident guess: 아직 회의 중일걸요. Use it when you have a hunch, not when you are simply unsure.

beginnerGuide.title: Open a careful possibility
beginnerGuide.body: -다면 sets up a what-if frame: 이미 나갔다면. It lets you discuss the next step without pretending you know the fact.

beginnerGuide.title: Soften the opinion itself
beginnerGuide.body: 것 같아요 softens a whole impression or opinion. Do not treat it as 같다 meaning 'same'; here it means 'it seems / I think.'

checkpoints: I can use -ㄹ걸요 for a careful guess without turning it into a wish.
I can use -다면 for a hypothetical condition and -(으)면 좋겠어요 for a gentle suggestion.
I can explain why 것 같아요 in this chapter is a hedge, not 'same.'

chapters.title: Irregular Verb Conjugation
chapters.goal: Apply the six major stem-change rules automatically so conjugated forms are always correct.
chapters.scenario: Fixing common learner mistakes like 춥어요, 듣어요, 모르어요, and 빨갛아요 by learning the stem changes behind everyday Korean.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.ko: 오늘 너무 추워요. 그런데 왜 '춥어요'가 아니에요?
dialogue.romanization: oneul neomu chuwoyo. geureonde wae 'chupeoyo'ga anieyo?
dialogue.en: It is so cold today. But why isn't it '춥어요'?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.ko: 춥다처럼 ㅂ으로 끝나는 말은 추워요, 더워요처럼 바뀌어요.
dialogue.romanization: chupdacheoreom bieubeuro kkeutnaneun mareun chuwoyo, deowoyo-cheoreom bakkwieoyo.
dialogue.en: Words ending in ㅂ, like 춥다, change to forms like 추워요 and 더워요.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.ko: 그럼 듣다는 들어요, 걷다는 걸어요가 맞죠?
dialogue.romanization: geureom deutdaneun deureoyo, geotdaneun georeoyoga matjyo?
dialogue.en: Then 듣다 becomes 들어요, and 걷다 becomes 걸어요, right?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.ko: 맞아요. 모르다는 몰라요, 빨갛다는 빨개요처럼 익히면 돼요.
dialogue.romanization: majayo. moreudaneun mollayo, ppalgataneun ppalgaeyo-cheoreom ikhimyeon dwaeyo.
dialogue.en: Right. Learn them as pairs, like 모르다 to 몰라요 and 빨갛다 to 빨개요.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.en: Got it. I will memorize the high-frequency words first.

chapters.guidedPractice: Convert ten dictionary forms into polite speech: 덥다, 춥다, 맵다, 듣다, 걷다, 묻다, 낫다, 모르다, 다르다, 빨갛다.
chapters.realLifeTask: Write a short weather, health, or study message using at least three changed forms such as 추워요, 어려워요, 들어요, 몰라요, or 어때요.
chapters.friendPractice: One person gives a dictionary form; the other says the polite form and names the rule before making a real sentence.
chapters.review: Can you spot why 춥어요, 듣어요, 모르어요, and 빨갛아요 sound wrong, then repair them quickly?

beginnerGuide.title: Change before vowel endings
beginnerGuide.body: Most changes happen when a vowel-starting ending arrives: 춥다 + 어요 becomes 추워요, 듣다 + 어요 becomes 들어요, and 모르다 + 아요 becomes 몰라요.

beginnerGuide.title: Learn useful pairs
beginnerGuide.body: Do not memorize rules alone. Memorize pairs you will actually say: 덥다/더워요, 어렵다/어려워요, 듣다/들어요, 걷다/걸어요, 모르다/몰라요, 어떻다/어때요.

beginnerGuide.title: Watch regular lookalikes
beginnerGuide.body: Not every final consonant changes. 듣다 becomes 들어요, but 닫다 stays 닫아요. 낫다 becomes 나아요, but 웃다 stays 웃어요.

checkpoints: I can correctly conjugate common ㅂ, ㄷ, ㅅ, 르, ㅎ, and ㄹ-deletion stems.
I can name at least one regular lookalike that does not change.
I can use irregular forms in real sentences, not only in a rule table.

chapters.title: Particle Expansion
chapters.goal: Use A2 particles to express recipient, togetherness, possession, also, only, nothing but, surprising amount, and at least.
chapters.scenario: Talking about weekend plans with particles: who you go with, what also happens, what is the only option, and what you can do at least for a short time.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.en: Are you also going to see a movie with a friend this weekend?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.ko: 아니요, 시험 문제가 세 개나 남아서 공부밖에 못 해요.
dialogue.romanization: aniyo, siheom munjega se gaena namaseo gongbubakke mot haeyo.
dialogue.en: No, as many as three exam questions are left, so I can only study.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.en: Then do you want to at least drink coffee? Just one hour.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.ko: 좋아요. 선생님께 이메일도 보내드리고, 친구의 책도 돌려줘야 해요.
dialogue.romanization: joayo. seonsaengnimkke imeildo bonaedeurigo, chinguui chaekdo dollyeojwoya haeyo.
dialogue.en: Sounds good. I also need to send the teacher an email and return my friend's book.

chapters.guidedPractice: Rewrite the same noun with three particles: 친구에게, 친구랑, 친구도; then contrast 공부만 해요 with 공부밖에 못 해요.
chapters.realLifeTask: Write a weekend-plan message using at least four particles from this chapter, including one recipient particle and one limit particle.
chapters.friendPractice: A partner gives a noun like 친구, 선생님, 커피, 시간, or 공부; answer with a sentence using 도, 만, 밖에, 이라도, or 에게/께.
chapters.review: Can you choose the right particle for also, only, receiver, possession, with, as many as, and at least without mixing their jobs?

beginnerGuide.title: Particles change the job
beginnerGuide.body: 친구 can become 친구에게 (to a friend), 친구랑 (with a friend), 친구도 (a friend too), 친구만 (only a friend), or 친구의 (a friend's). The noun is the same; the relationship changes.

beginnerGuide.title: 만 and 밖에 are not twins
beginnerGuide.body: 공부만 해요 is neutral: I only study. 공부밖에 못 해요 needs a negative predicate and feels limited: I can do nothing but study.

beginnerGuide.title: 이라도 gives a minimum option
beginnerGuide.body: 커피라도 마실래요? means coffee is not the full plan, but it is at least something possible. It is different from 커피만 and 커피도.

checkpoints: I can use 에게/한테/께 for people who receive an action.
I can contrast 도, 만, 밖에, 이나, and 이라도 in real sentences.
I can use 의 or drop it naturally when talking about possession.

chapters.title: Counters and Classifiers
chapters.goal: Count people, objects, animals, books, sheets, cups, clothing sets, machines, and occurrences using the correct classifier and number system.
chapters.scenario: Preparing a small class event: counting students, a dog, chairs, drinks, paper sheets, guide books, and how many times the event has happened.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.ko: 오늘 체험 수업에 학생 몇 명 와요?
dialogue.romanization: oneul cheheom sueobe haksaeng myeot myeong wayo?
dialogue.en: How many students are coming to today's trial class?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.ko: 학생 세 명이 오고, 강아지 한 마리도 데려온대요.
dialogue.romanization: haksaeng se myeongi ogo, gangaji han marido deryeondaeyo.
dialogue.en: Three students are coming, and they say they are bringing one dog too.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.ko: 그럼 의자 네 개랑 커피 네 잔 준비할게요.
dialogue.romanization: geureom uija ne gaerang keopi ne jan junbihalgeyo.
dialogue.en: Then I will prepare four chairs and four cups of coffee.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.en: How many sheets of paper do we need?

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.ko: 열 장이면 돼요. 안내 책도 두 권만 주세요.
dialogue.romanization: yeol jangimyeon dwaeyo. annae chaekdo du gwonman juseyo.
dialogue.en: Ten sheets are enough. Please give me just two guide books too.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.ko: 이 준비는 벌써 세 번 해 봐서 괜찮아요.
dialogue.romanization: i junbineun beolsseo se beon hae bwaseo gwaenchanayo.
dialogue.en: We have already done this prep three times, so it is fine.

chapters.guidedPractice: Make one sentence each with 명, 개, 마리, 잔, 권, 장, 벌, 대, and 번, then check whether the number should be native or Sino-Korean.
chapters.realLifeTask: Write a real shopping, cafe, class, or pet-care message with at least four counters from this chapter.
chapters.friendPractice: A partner gives you a noun like 학생, 커피, 책, 종이, 옷, 사진, or 강아지; answer with the correct counter and a full sentence.
chapters.review: Can you choose the counter first, then pick the correct number shape: 한/두/세/네/스무 vs 일/이/삼?

beginnerGuide.title: Noun + number + counter
beginnerGuide.body: Most everyday counting uses the noun first, then number plus counter: 학생 세 명, 커피 두 잔, 책 두 권, 종이 열 장.

beginnerGuide.title: Native number changes
beginnerGuide.body: Before counters, 하나/둘/셋/넷/스물 become 한/두/세/네/스무: 한 개, 두 잔, 세 명, 네 장, 스무 명.

beginnerGuide.title: Not every counter uses native numbers
beginnerGuide.body: Everyday object counters use native numbers, but some units use Sino-Korean numbers, especially 번 for sequence or repeated actions in many contexts: 세 번, 일 번.

checkpoints: I can match common nouns with counters: 학생 세 명, 강아지 한 마리, 책 두 권, 종이 열 장.
I can use 한/두/세/네/스무 before native-number counters.
I can distinguish counting items from counting occurrences with 번.

chapters.title: Pronunciation Rules
chapters.goal: Predict and produce the spoken form of any written Korean word by applying the four core phonological rules.
chapters.scenario: Mapping written Hangul to real speech: liaison, tensification, nasalization, and aspiration in everyday words.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.en: 먹어요 is not [meok-eo-yo]; it links and sounds like [머거요].

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.en: Why do 학교 and 국밥 sound like [학꾜] and [국빱]?

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.en: It is because a tense sound appears after the final consonant.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.en: Then 국민 sounds like [궁민], and 먹는 sounds like [멍는], right?

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.ko: 맞아요. 좋다와 입학은 [조타], [이팍]처럼 ㅎ 때문에 세게 나요.
dialogue.romanization: majayo. jotdawa iphak-eun [jota], [ipak]cheoreom hieut ttaemune sege nayo.
dialogue.en: Right. 좋다 and 입학 become stronger sounds like [조타] and [이팍] because of ㅎ.

chapters.guidedPractice: Mark the spoken form for eight words: 먹어요, 한국어, 앉아요, 학교, 국밥, 국민, 좋다, 입학.
chapters.realLifeTask: Record or read aloud five sentences containing one liaison example, one tense-sound example, one nasalization example, and one aspiration example.
chapters.friendPractice: A partner gives you a written word; say the likely spoken form and name the rule before reading the full sentence.
chapters.review: Can you explain why 먹어요, 학교, 국민, and 좋다 are not pronounced exactly block by block?

beginnerGuide.title: Hangul is regular, speech is connected
beginnerGuide.body: Korean spelling is reliable, but spoken Korean connects blocks: 먹어요 is read closer to [머거요], and 한국어 is read closer to [한구거].

beginnerGuide.title: Blocked sounds can push the next sound
beginnerGuide.body: After a final consonant, the next plain sound can become tense: 학교 [학꾜], 국밥 [국빱], 먹고 [먹꼬].

beginnerGuide.title: Nasals and ㅎ change neighbors
beginnerGuide.body: Before ㄴ/ㅁ, stops often become nasal: 국민 [궁민]. When ㅎ meets a stop, it often makes an aspirated sound: 좋다 [조타], 입학 [이팍].

checkpoints: I can identify liaison in words like 먹어요, 한국어, 앉아요, and 읽어요.
I can identify tensification and nasalization in 학교, 국밥, 국민, and 먹는.
I can identify aspiration in 좋다, 축하해요, 입학, and 못해요.

chapters.title: Negation Deep Dive
chapters.goal: Distinguish all four negation strategies and choose the correct one based on ability, choice, and politeness register.
