chapters.scenario: Declining an invitation, explaining a dietary restriction, and saying something cannot be done versus will not be done.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.ko: 오늘 모임에는 못 가요. 시간이 없어요.
dialogue.romanization: oneul moimeneun mot gayo. sigani eopseoyo.
dialogue.en: I cannot go to the gathering today. I do not have time.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.ko: 안 가는 거예요, 아니면 정말 못 가는 거예요?
dialogue.romanization: an ganeun geoyeyo, animyeon jeongmal mot ganeun geoyeyo?
dialogue.en: Are you choosing not to go, or are you really unable to go?

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.ko: 가기 싫은 건 아니에요. 야근 때문에 못 가요.
dialogue.romanization: gagi silheun geon anieyo. yageun ttaemune mot gayo.
dialogue.en: It is not that I do not want to go. I cannot go because of overtime.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.en: Then at the company dinner, do you not eat meat?

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.ko: 싫어서 안 먹는 게 아니라 알레르기가 있어서 못 먹어요.
dialogue.romanization: silheoseo an meongneun ge anira allereugiga isseoseo mot meogeoyo.
dialogue.en: It is not that I avoid it because I dislike it; I cannot eat it because I have an allergy.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.ko: 그럼 어렵지 않게 다른 메뉴로 예약할게요.
dialogue.romanization: geureom eoryeopji anke dareun menyuro yeyakhalgeyo.
dialogue.en: Then I will reserve a different menu so it is not difficult.

chapters.guidedPractice: Make four short explanations: one with 안, one with 못, one with -지 않아요, and one with N이/가 없어요.
chapters.realLifeTask: Draft a polite refusal that explains whether the issue is choice, inability, no time, or a careful clarification.
chapters.friendPractice: A partner gives you a situation such as invitation, food restriction, homework, or phone call; answer with 안, 못, -지 않다, or 없다 and explain why.
chapters.review: Can you tell the difference between 안 가요, 못 가요, 가지 않아요, and 시간이 없어요 without using English 'not' for all of them?

beginnerGuide.title: Choice or blocked situation
beginnerGuide.body: 안 가요 can sound like a choice. 못 가요 says something blocks you: time, ability, rules, schedule, or health.

beginnerGuide.title: No thing, no time, no option
beginnerGuide.body: N이/가 없어요 is not just a vocabulary phrase. It is a negation strategy for absence: 시간이 없어요, 돈이 없어요, 방법이 없어요.

beginnerGuide.title: Careful or written negation
beginnerGuide.body: -지 않아요 sounds more careful than short 안. It is useful for clarification: 싫지 않아요, 어렵지 않아요, 먹지 않아요.

checkpoints: I can use 안 for choice or simple factual negation.
I can use 못 for inability, schedule blocks, rules, or health restrictions.
I can use 없다 and -지 않다 for absence and careful clarification.

chapters.title: 이다 Deep Dive
chapters.goal: Use 이다 in past tense, as a connective, as a reason clause, and as a concessive/minimal-option marker.
chapters.scenario: Talking about past and current roles, then using time nouns like weekend, weekday, and morning to explain why a study plan is possible or limited.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.en: Were you a student last year?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.en: Even though I am an office worker now, I keep studying.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.en: Because you are an office worker, do you need Korean more?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.ko: 네. 평일에는 바쁘니까 아침에만 조금 해요.
dialogue.romanization: ne. pyeongireneun bappeunikka achimenman jogeum haeyo.
dialogue.en: Yes. Since weekdays are busy, I only do a little in the morning.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.ko: 그럼 주말이니까 한 시간이라도 같이 공부해요.
dialogue.romanization: geureom jumarinikka han siganirado gachi gongbuhaeyo.
dialogue.en: Then since it is the weekend, let's study together even if just for one hour.

chapters.guidedPractice: Choose one role noun and one time noun, then make five sentences: past identity, background, reason with 라서, reason with 니까, and a fallback with 라도.
chapters.realLifeTask: Send or say one sentence about your real schedule, such as 주말이니까 한 시간이라도 공부해요.
chapters.friendPractice: A partner asks about your role or schedule; answer with 학생이었어요, 회사원인데요, 주말이라서, 주말이니까, or 한 시간이라도.
chapters.review: Can you explain why 학생, 회사원, 주말, 평일, 아침, and 시간 fit this chapter better than random nouns?

beginnerGuide.title: 이다 changes nouns into sentence material
beginnerGuide.body: This chapter should start from nouns that naturally become identity or schedule explanations: 학생이었어요, 회사원인데요, 주말이라서, 평일이니까.

beginnerGuide.title: 라서 explains; 니까 often leads to action
beginnerGuide.body: 회사원이라서 한국어가 필요해요 simply explains the cause. 주말이니까 공부해요 sounds more like a reason for a decision or suggestion.

beginnerGuide.title: 라도 is the fallback marker
beginnerGuide.body: 한 시간이라도 공부해요 means one hour is not ideal, but it is still worth doing. That is why 시간 is a useful core noun here.

checkpoints: I can say a past role with N이었어요/였어요.
I can use N인데요 or N인데도 to give background before the main point.
I can choose between N이라서, N이니까, and N이라도 based on explanation, decision, or fallback.

chapters.title: Family and Honorific Kinship Terms
chapters.goal: Name and address family members correctly in both plain and honorific registers, and talk about relationships.
chapters.scenario: Introducing family size, choosing sibling terms by speaker gender, and using honorific subject language when parents or grandparents come to an event.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.en: How many people are in your family?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.ko: 저희 가족은 다섯 명이에요. 부모님하고 형, 동생이 있어요.
dialogue.romanization: jeohui gajogeun daseot myeongieyo. bumonimhago hyeong, dongsaengi isseoyo.
dialogue.en: There are five people in my family. I have my parents, an older brother, and a younger sibling.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.en: Hyeong is the word a male speaker uses, right?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.ko: 네. 여자가 부르면 오빠라고 해요. 누나와 언니도 달라요.
dialogue.romanization: ne. yeojaga bureumyeon opparago haeyo. nuna-wa eonnido dallayo.
dialogue.en: Yes. If a female speaker says it, she says oppa. Nuna and eonni are different too.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.en: Are your parents coming to the wedding too?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.en: Yes, my mother is coming, and my father is coming too.

chapters.guidedPractice: Introduce your family size, name two family members, then make one honorific sentence with 께서 and one sibling-term sentence with 형/오빠 or 누나/언니.
chapters.realLifeTask: Write a polite self-introduction sentence such as 저희 가족은 네 명이에요, then add one sentence about 부모님께서 or 할머니께서.
chapters.friendPractice: A partner gives a speaker gender and an older sibling; choose 형, 오빠, 누나, or 언니, then make a family-size sentence.
chapters.review: Can you explain why 저희, 명, 부모님, 형/오빠/누나/언니, and 께서 belong together in this chapter?

beginnerGuide.title: Count people with 명, not 개
beginnerGuide.body: 가족이 몇 명이에요? and 저희 가족은 네 명이에요 are the base sentences. People take 명, and the number before 명 is native Korean: 한, 두, 세, 네, 다섯.

beginnerGuide.title: Sibling terms depend on the speaker
beginnerGuide.body: A male speaker says 형 for an older brother and 누나 for an older sister. A female speaker says 오빠 and 언니. 동생 works for a younger sibling.

beginnerGuide.title: Honor the subject with 께서 and -(으)시-
beginnerGuide.body: 부모님께서 오세요 and 어머니께서 오셨어요 honor the person doing the action. 께서 is for the subject; 께 without 서 marks a respected receiver.

checkpoints: I can introduce family size with 저희 가족은 ~ 명이에요.
I can choose 형, 오빠, 누나, or 언니 from the speaker's point of view.
I can use 께서 with an honorific verb form for parents, grandparents, teachers, or elders.

chapters.title: Health and Body
chapters.goal: Describe physical symptoms, navigate a clinic or pharmacy, and follow a doctor's basic instructions.
chapters.scenario: A learner visits a neighborhood clinic, explains fever, cough, throat or stomach pain, receives a prescription, and understands after-meal medicine instructions at the pharmacy.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.en: Where does it hurt? What brings you in?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.ko: 아침부터 열이 나고 목이 아파요. 기침도 나요.
dialogue.romanization: achimbuteo yeori nago mogi apayo. gichimdo nayo.
dialogue.en: Since this morning I have had a fever and a sore throat. I also have a cough.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.ko: 감기 때문에 그런 것 같아요. 약은 식후에 하루 세 번 드셔야 해요.
dialogue.romanization: gamgi ttaemune geureon geot gatayo. yageun sikhue haru se beon deusyeoya haeyo.
dialogue.en: It seems to be because of a cold. You have to take the medicine three times a day after meals.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.ko: 기침 때문에 잠을 못 자면 다시 와야 하나요?
dialogue.romanization: gichim ttaemune jameul mot jamyeon dasi waya hanayo?
dialogue.en: If I cannot sleep because of the cough, should I come back?

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.ko: 네. 열이 계속 나니까 물을 많이 마시고 쉬세요.
dialogue.romanization: ne. yeori gyesok nanikka mureul mani masigo swiseyo.
dialogue.en: Yes. Since the fever is continuing, drink a lot of water and rest.

chapters.guidedPractice: Make one clinic line for each step: symptom, cause, instruction, warning sign, and pharmacy direction.
chapters.realLifeTask: Write a short message you could show at a clinic: 아침부터 열이 나고 목이 아파요. 기침 때문에 잠을 못 잤어요.
chapters.friendPractice: A partner gives a symptom card; answer with a clinic sentence and one medicine instruction using 식후 or 하루 세 번.
chapters.review: Can you connect symptoms, causes, and instructions without mixing up 열이 나다, 기침이 나다, 아프다, 때문에, and 식후?

beginnerGuide.title: Symptoms often use 이/가
beginnerGuide.body: 목이 아파요, 배가 아파요, 열이 나요, 기침이 나요. The body part or symptom usually becomes the subject.

beginnerGuide.title: Clinic and pharmacy words belong together
beginnerGuide.body: 병원에서 의사에게 증상을 말하고 처방전을 받아요. 약국에서는 약사에게 약 먹는 시간과 식후 지시를 확인해요.

beginnerGuide.title: Instructions need clear timing
beginnerGuide.body: 약은 식후에 하루 세 번 드셔야 해요 means after meals, three times a day. 식후 is not a random health word; it is the timing word on medicine labels.

checkpoints: I can describe symptoms with body part or symptom + 이/가 + 아프다/나다.
I can explain a cause with 때문에, 아파서, or 니까 in a clinic sentence.
I can understand basic medicine directions with 식후, 하루, 번, and -아/어야 해요.

chapters.title: Housing and Daily Living
chapters.goal: Describe a home's layout, discuss neighborhood amenities, and handle basic landlord/real-estate interactions.
chapters.scenario: A newcomer views a studio through a real-estate office, checks deposit, monthly rent, maintenance fees, included utilities, and the contract before moving.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.en: How much is the deposit for this studio?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.en: The deposit is 5 million won and the monthly rent is 700,000 won.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.en: Is the maintenance fee separate? Is internet included too?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.en: The maintenance fee is 70,000 won, and internet is included.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.ko: 이사하기 전에 계약서를 확인해 두면 되죠?
dialogue.romanization: isahagi jeone gyeyakseoreul hwaginhae dumyeon doejyo?
dialogue.en: I should check the contract before moving, right?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.ko: 네. 마음에 들면 오늘 계약할 수 있어요.
dialogue.romanization: ne. maeume deulmyeon oneul gyeyakal su isseoyo.
dialogue.en: Yes. If you like it, you can sign the contract today.

chapters.guidedPractice: Make five real-estate sentences: layout, deposit/monthly rent, separate fees, included utilities, and contract preparation.
chapters.realLifeTask: Write a message you could send about a listing: 보증금은 500만 원이고 월세는 70만 원이에요. 관리비에 인터넷이 포함돼 있어요.
chapters.friendPractice: A partner plays the agent; ask about 보증금, 월세, 관리비, 포함 여부, and 계약서.
chapters.review: Can you explain why 원룸, 부동산, 보증금, 월세, 관리비, 포함되다, 따로, and 계약서 belong together in one housing task?

beginnerGuide.title: Housing price has more than one number
beginnerGuide.body: A Korean listing often gives 보증금 and 월세 together. 월세만 물어보면 실제 비용을 놓칠 수 있어요.

beginnerGuide.title: 관리비 changes the real monthly cost
beginnerGuide.body: 관리비는 따로예요? 인터넷도 포함돼 있어요? 공과금이나 인터넷이 포함되는지에 따라 실제 월 비용이 달라져요.

beginnerGuide.title: Prepare before signing
beginnerGuide.body: 이사하기 전에 계약서를 확인해 두세요. -아/어 두다 fits this chapter because it means doing a task in advance and leaving it ready.

checkpoints: I can ask about 보증금, 월세, 관리비, and included utilities.
I can describe a room with adjective modifiers like 넓은 원룸 and 깨끗한 화장실.
I can use 조건/가능/준비 patterns for housing decisions: 마음에 들면, 계약할 수 있어요, 확인해 두세요.

chapters.title: Weather and Seasons
chapters.goal: Describe current weather and seasonal conditions, make weather-related plans, and understand forecast language.
chapters.scenario: A learner checks the weekend forecast before planning a trip to Jeju, discusses typhoon warnings with a coworker, and texts a friend about canceling outdoor plans due to fine dust.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.en: Did you see the weekend forecast?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.ko: 태풍이 올 것 같아서 비행기가 늦을 수도 있어요.
dialogue.romanization: taepungi ol geot gataseo bihaenggiga neujeul sudo isseoyo.
dialogue.en: It looks like a typhoon may come, so the plane might be late.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.ko: 미세먼지가 심하면 일정은 취소하는 게 좋겠어요.
dialogue.romanization: misemeonjiga simhamyeon iljeongeun chwisohaneun ge jotgesseoyo.
dialogue.en: If the fine dust is bad, it would be better to cancel the plan.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.en: Let's book again when the weather clears.

chapters.guidedPractice: Make five forecast-plan sentences: prediction, concern, condition, cause, and timing.
chapters.realLifeTask: Write a real weather-plan text: 태풍이 올 것 같아서 일정을 미루는 게 좋겠어요.
chapters.friendPractice: A partner gives a forecast; decide whether to bring an umbrella, cancel, delay, or rebook.
chapters.review: Can you connect 일기예보, 태풍, 미세먼지, 비/눈, 우산, 일정, 취소하다, and 다시 예약하다 in one real plan?

beginnerGuide.title: Forecast language changes plans
beginnerGuide.body: 일기예보를 보고 비가 올 것 같아요, 태풍이 올 텐데요, 미세먼지 때문에 취소해요처럼 계획을 조정해요.

beginnerGuide.title: 비 and 눈 both use 오다
beginnerGuide.body: 비가 와요 and 눈이 와요 use the same everyday verb 오다. 날씨의 눈은 eye가 아니라 snow예요.

beginnerGuide.title: 미세먼지 is plan vocabulary
beginnerGuide.body: Korean daily plans often change because of 미세먼지, 황사, 태풍, 장마, or 소나기. Weather words should connect to 일정 and 취소하다.

checkpoints: I can make a cautious forecast with -(으)ㄹ 것 같아요 or -(으)ㄹ 텐데.
I can explain plan changes with N 때문에 and V면.
I can use V(으)ㄹ 때 for weather timing such as 비가 올 때 or 날씨가 맑아질 때.

chapters.title: Clothing and Appearance
chapters.goal: Shop for clothing confidently, describe outfits and personal style, and navigate Korean fashion retail language.
chapters.scenario: A learner goes to a clothing store at 명동, asks about sizes and fitting rooms, returns a defective item, and later describes what to wear for a job interview to a Korean friend.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.en: May I try on this shirt?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.en: Yes, the fitting room is on the right.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.ko: 조금 커 보여요. 한 치수 작은 것도 보여 주시겠어요?
dialogue.romanization: jogeum keo boyeoyo. han chisu jageun geotdo boyeo jusigesseoyo?
dialogue.en: It looks a little big. Could you show me one size smaller too?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.ko: 네. 면접에는 이 셔츠보다 남색 셔츠가 더 단정해 보여요.
dialogue.romanization: ne. myeonjeobeneun i syeocheuboda namsaek syeocheuga deo danjeonghae boyeoyo.
dialogue.en: Sure. For an interview, the navy shirt looks neater than this shirt.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.ko: 그럼 이걸로 할게요. 교환이나 환불도 돼요?
dialogue.romanization: geureom igeollo halgeyo. gyohwanina hwanbuldo dwaeyo?
dialogue.en: Then I'll take this one. Can I exchange or refund it too?

chapters.guidedPractice: Build five shop sentences: try on, ask another size, describe fit, compare interview options, and ask exchange/refund policy.
chapters.realLifeTask: Write a real store message: 사이즈가 조금 커서 한 치수 작은 것도 보여 주시겠어요?
chapters.friendPractice: A partner chooses an outfit situation; answer with 잘 어울려요, 커 보여요, 단정해 보여요, or 교환돼요?
chapters.review: Can you separate size fit (맞다/크다/작다), appearance (어울리다/보이다), and store policy (교환/환불)?

beginnerGuide.title: Fit and style are different
beginnerGuide.body: 사이즈가 맞아요 means the size fits. 잘 어울려요 means it suits the person. 커 보여요 or 작아 보여요 describes how it looks.

beginnerGuide.title: Store requests need soft endings
beginnerGuide.body: 입어 봐도 돼요? asks permission to try on. 보여 주시겠어요? is a polite staff request for another size or color.

beginnerGuide.title: Interview clothing uses 단정하다
beginnerGuide.body: For interviews or work, 단정해 보여요 is often more useful than 예뻐요 because it means neat, presentable, and appropriate.

checkpoints: I can ask to try on clothing and ask where the fitting room is.
I can ask for one size smaller/larger with 한 치수 작은/큰 거.
I can distinguish 잘 어울려요, 사이즈가 맞아요, and 단정해 보여요.

chapters.title: Korean Food Culture
chapters.goal: Discuss cooking methods and ingredients, read a restaurant menu in depth, and talk about food preferences and Korean dining customs.
chapters.scenario: A learner joins Korean coworkers at a 삼겹살 restaurant, orders confidently, participates in grilling at the table, and later explains a Korean dish to a non-Korean friend.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.ko: 삼겹살 두 인분하고 공기밥 하나 주세요.
dialogue.romanization: samgyeopsal du inbunhago gonggibap hana juseyo.
dialogue.en: Please give us two servings of samgyeopsal and one bowl of rice.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.en: Please give us a little more side dishes too.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.en: Let's grill the meat and the garlic together too.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.en: The meat is cooked now, so please cut it.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.en: Please pack the leftovers to go.

chapters.guidedPractice: Build five restaurant sentences: order servings, ask for side dishes, describe grilling, request cutting, and pack leftovers.
chapters.realLifeTask: Write a real barbecue order: 삼겹살 두 인분하고 공기밥 하나 주세요.
chapters.friendPractice: A partner runs the table grill; say when to grill, cut, add rice, or pack leftovers.
chapters.review: Can you connect 인분, 공기밥, 밑반찬, 굽다, 익다, 자르다, and 포장해 주세요 in one restaurant flow?

beginnerGuide.title: 인분 counts servings, not people
beginnerGuide.body: 삼겹살 두 인분 is two servings of pork belly. 두 명 is two people, so do not use 명 when ordering portions.

beginnerGuide.title: Grilling has action and result words
beginnerGuide.body: 굽다 is the action of grilling. 익다 is the result: 고기가 익었어요. When it is cooked, you can say 잘라 주세요.

beginnerGuide.title: Requests split into item and action
beginnerGuide.body: N 주세요 orders an item: 공기밥 주세요. V아/어 주세요 asks for an action: 잘라 주세요, 포장해 주세요.

checkpoints: I can order meat by 인분 and rice as 공기밥.
I can say 고기를 굽다, 고기가 익다, and 고기를 자르다 correctly.
I can ask for more side dishes or leftovers with 주세요 forms.

chapters.title: Entertainment and Digital Life
chapters.goal: Discuss K-dramas, K-pop, and social media using natural Korean vocabulary, and navigate smartphone and streaming app interactions.
chapters.scenario: A learner recommends a K-drama to a Korean friend on KakaoTalk, discusses a K-pop idol, and asks for help with a streaming app that keeps buffering.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.en: Have you watched this drama before?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.ko: 네. 배우도 좋지만 댓글이 진짜 재미있거든요.
dialogue.romanization: ne. baeudo jojiman daetgeuri jinjja jaemiitgeodeunyo.
dialogue.en: Yes. The actor is good too, but the comments are really fun, you know.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.ko: 친구가 자막이 좋다고 했어요. 영상도 공유했어요?
dialogue.romanization: chinguga jamagi jotago haesseoyo. yeongsangdo gongyuhaesseoyo?
dialogue.en: My friend said the subtitles are good. Did you share the video too?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.en: I shared it, but the video keeps cutting out.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.ko: 와이파이를 다시 연결해 보세요. 좋아요도 눌렀어요?
dialogue.romanization: waipaireul dasi yeongyeolhae boseyo. joayodo nulleosseoyo?
dialogue.en: Try reconnecting the Wi-Fi. Did you hit like too?

chapters.guidedPractice: Build five digital-life sentences: drama experience, comment reaction, reported subtitle opinion, shared video, and buffering fix.
chapters.realLifeTask: Send a real recommendation-style message: 이 드라마 본 적 있어요? 댓글이 진짜 재미있거든요.
chapters.friendPractice: A partner describes a video or app issue; respond with 자막, 공유하다, 끊기다, 와이파이, or 좋아요를 누르다.
chapters.review: Can you connect 드라마, 댓글, 자막, 영상, 공유하다, 끊기다, 와이파이, and 좋아요 눌렀어요 in one natural chat?

beginnerGuide.title: Drama talk starts with experience
beginnerGuide.body: 이 드라마 본 적 있어요? asks whether someone has watched it before. Use 봤어요 for a specific past time, but 본 적 있어요 for experience.

beginnerGuide.title: Digital reactions are short
beginnerGuide.body: 댓글이 재미있어요, 대박, 헐, ㅋㅋ, 좋아요 눌렀어요 are real chat pieces. They should connect to the content, not float as random slang.

beginnerGuide.title: Streaming problems use 끊기다
beginnerGuide.body: 영상이 끊겨요 or 와이파이가 끊겼어요 describes buffering or disconnection. 끊다 is active; 끊기다 is the problem happening.

checkpoints: I can ask about watching experience with 본 적 있어요.
I can report someone else's opinion with -다고 했어요.
I can describe a buffering video and suggest reconnecting Wi-Fi.

chapters.title: Education and School Life
chapters.goal: Navigate Korean school and university contexts, discuss study habits and exams, and understand the cultural weight of academic achievement.
chapters.scenario: A learner enrolls in a Korean language school, asks a classmate about the upcoming 중간고사, discusses study schedules, and explains their educational background to a Korean acquaintance.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.ko: 중간고사 전에 발표 과제를 끝내야 해요?
dialogue.romanization: junggangosa jeone balpyo gwajereul kkeutnaeya haeyo?
dialogue.en: Do we have to finish the presentation assignment before the midterm?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.ko: 네, 이번 학기 성적에 들어가니까 준비해야 해요.
dialogue.romanization: ne, ibeon hakgi seongjeoge deureoganikka junbihaeya haeyo.
dialogue.en: Yes, it counts toward this semester's grade, so we have to prepare.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.ko: 그럼 오늘부터 도서관에서 공부하기 시작하기로 했어요.
dialogue.romanization: geureom oneulbuteo doseogwaneseo gongbuhagi sijakagiro haesseoyo.
dialogue.en: Then I decided to start studying at the library from today.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.ko: 기말고사에서 좋은 성적을 받기 위해 시험 기간 동안 매일 공부해야 해요.
dialogue.romanization: gimalgosaeseo joeun seongjeogeul batgi wihae siheom gigan dongan maeil gongbuhaeya haeyo.
dialogue.en: In order to get a good grade on the final exam, we have to study every day during exam period.

chapters.guidedPractice: Build five school-life sentences: assignment obligation, class decision, study start, exam-period duration, and purpose for getting a good grade.
chapters.realLifeTask: Write a real classmate message: 중간고사 전에 발표 과제를 끝내야 해요?
chapters.friendPractice: A partner gives a school deadline; answer with 과제, 중간고사, 기말고사, 도서관, or 공부해야 해요.
chapters.review: Can you connect 과제, 발표하다, 중간고사, 학기, 성적, 도서관, 공부하다, 받다, and 동안 in one school plan?

beginnerGuide.title: Assignments connect to exams
beginnerGuide.body: 과제, 발표, 중간고사, 기말고사 are not random school words. They form a deadline chain: 과제를 끝내야 해요, 중간고사 전에, 기말고사에서 좋은 성적을 받기 위해.

beginnerGuide.title: 동안 is a study-period word
beginnerGuide.body: 시험 기간 동안, 한 학기 동안, 방학 동안 all describe a stretch of time. Do not use 에 for this duration meaning.

beginnerGuide.title: Purpose sounds deliberate
beginnerGuide.body: 합격하기 위해 공부해요 sounds more planned than just 공부해요. Use it for serious goals like exams, scholarships, or graduation.

checkpoints: I can talk about assignment deadlines with V아/어야 해요.
I can report a study decision with V기로 했어요.
I can use N 동안 and V기 위해서 in exam-study plans.

chapters.title: Transportation in Depth
chapters.goal: Navigate Korea's public transit system independently, including subway line transfers, bus routes, taxis, and KTX train booking.
chapters.scenario: A learner travels from Hongik University station to Busan by KTX, using the subway to reach Seoul Station, buys a KTX ticket at the counter, and texts a friend about a delayed bus.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.en: Where do I transfer if I want to get to Seoul Station?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.romanization: i hoseoneul tago sicheongyeogeseo il hoseoneuro garataseyo. seunggangjangeun ijjogiyeyo.
dialogue.en: Take Line 2 and transfer to Line 1 at City Hall Station. The platform is this way.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.ko: 부산 가는 KTX 표를 예매하려고 해요. 편도랑 왕복 중에 뭐가 나아요?
dialogue.romanization: busan ganeun KTX pyoreul yemaeharyeogo haeyo. pyeondorang wangbok junge mwoga naayo?
dialogue.en: I am trying to book a KTX ticket to Busan. Which is better, one-way or round-trip?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.ko: 돌아오는 시간이 정해지지 않았으면 편도로 예매하세요. 매진이면 다음 기차를 확인하세요.
dialogue.romanization: doraoneun sigani jeonghaejiji anasseumyeon pyeondoro yemaehaseyo. maejinimyeon daeum gichareul hwaginhaseyo.
dialogue.en: If the return time is not set, book it one-way. If it is sold out, check the next train.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.ko: 버스 지연 때문에 늦으면 택시로 갈게요.
dialogue.romanization: beoseu jiyeon ttaemune neujeumyeon taeksiro galgeyo.
dialogue.en: If I am late because of a bus delay, I will go by taxi.

chapters.guidedPractice: Write route, transfer, booking, and delay sentences: one with N(으)로, one with V(으)려고 해요, one with V면, one with N 때문에, and one with V(으)ㄹ 때.
chapters.realLifeTask: Open a map or train app and say one real route sentence, one ticket sentence, and one delay sentence aloud.
chapters.friendPractice: A partner asks how to get to Seoul Station or Busan; answer with transfer, platform, ticket, or delay vocabulary.
chapters.review: Can you separate 환승하다, 갈아타다, 예매하다, 매진, 지연, and N(으)로 in one travel plan?

beginnerGuide.title: Follow the trip order
beginnerGuide.body: Start with the subway route, then the transfer point, then the KTX ticket, then the delay plan. The vocabulary should match that order.

beginnerGuide.title: Use the right transport word
beginnerGuide.body: 환승 is the transfer event or system discount; 갈아타다 is the action of changing vehicles or lines. KTX tickets are usually 예매하다, and sold-out tickets are 매진.

beginnerGuide.title: Check particles
beginnerGuide.body: Use 에서 for the transfer place, 으로/로 for the line or means, 때문에 for the delay cause, and 때 for the moment you book or transfer.

checkpoints: I can ask where to transfer and answer with a line number or platform.
I can book a KTX ticket using 예매하다, 편도, 왕복, and 매진.
I can explain a delay plan with 지연 때문에, V면, and 택시로.

chapters.title: Korean Social Customs
chapters.goal: Understand and participate in Korean social rituals around age, titles, gift-giving, and group harmony (눈치), avoiding common social missteps.
chapters.scenario: A learner attends a Korean coworker's housewarming party (집들이), brings an appropriate gift, correctly uses titles when addressing elders, and reads the social atmosphere to know when to offer to help and when to stay quiet.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.ko: 집들이에 갈 때 휴지랑 세제 중에 뭐가 나아요?
dialogue.romanization: jipdeurie gal ttae hyujirang seje junge mwoga naayo?
dialogue.en: When going to a housewarming, which is better, toilet paper or detergent?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.ko: 둘 다 괜찮아요. 집들이 선물로 많이 가져가잖아요.
dialogue.romanization: dul da gwaenchanayo. jipdeuri seonmullo manhi gajyeogajanhayo.
dialogue.en: Both are fine. People often bring them as housewarming gifts, you know.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.en: If we are about the same age, can I say we are the same age?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.ko: 그래도 처음엔 선배님 같은 호칭을 쓰는 편이에요.
dialogue.romanization: geuraedo cheoeumen seonbaenim gateun hochingeul sseuneun pyeonieyo.
dialogue.en: Even so, at first people tend to use a title like seonbaenim.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.en: If elders are there too, I will ask, 'May I help?'

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.ko: 좋아요. 눈치 있게 챙기면 분위기가 덜 어색해요.
dialogue.romanization: joayo. nunchi itge chaenggimyeon bunwigiga deol eosaekaeyo.
dialogue.en: Good. If you take care of things tactfully, the mood is less awkward.

chapters.guidedPractice: Write one sentence for a housewarming gift, one title/age sentence, one 눈치 sentence, one polite help offer, and one gratitude sentence with 덕분에.
chapters.realLifeTask: Practice a short housewarming message: say what gift you will bring, how you will address people, and how you will offer help.
chapters.friendPractice: A partner describes who is at the 집들이; choose a title, gift, and polite action that fits the atmosphere.
chapters.review: Can you explain why 나이, 호칭, 선배/후배, 어르신, 눈치, and 덕분에 belong together in this chapter?

beginnerGuide.title: Start from the room
beginnerGuide.body: At a 집들이, first notice who is there: coworkers, 선배, 후배, 동갑, or 어르신. That decides the 호칭 and speech level.

beginnerGuide.title: Gift words are practical
beginnerGuide.body: 휴지 and 세제 are common 집들이 선물 because they are useful household items. The point is not the object alone; it is showing consideration.

beginnerGuide.title: 눈치 is action
beginnerGuide.body: 눈치 is not only 'reading the room.' It becomes language through 도와드릴까요?, 먼저 하세요, 수고하셨습니다, and 덕분에.

checkpoints: I can choose a housewarming gift word and explain why it fits.
I can use 호칭, 선배/후배, 동갑, and 어르신 without sounding too casual.
I can offer help and thank someone with 눈치, 챙기다, 도와드리다, 수고하셨습니다, and 덕분에.

chapters.title: Causative Verbs
chapters.goal: Produce and distinguish morphological causatives (사동사) from their base forms and from passive constructions, covering the seven main suffixes.
chapters.scenario: A parent tells a child to eat, a teacher has students read aloud, a manager asks staff to sit — all situations where the subject causes another person to perform an action.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.en: I fed the child and gave them medicine too.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.en: Did you put the baby to sleep and put a coat on them too?

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.ko: 네. 선생님은 학생들에게 본문을 읽히고 앞자리에 앉혔어요.
dialogue.romanization: ne. seonsaengnimeun haksaengdeurege bonmuneul ilkigo apjarie anjhyeosseoyo.
dialogue.en: Yes. The teacher had the students read the passage and seated them in the front row.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.ko: 그 농담은 모두를 웃겼고, 그 영화는 저를 울렸어요.
dialogue.romanization: geu nongdameun modureul utgyeotgo, geu yeonghwaneun jeoreul ullyeosseoyo.
dialogue.en: That joke made everyone laugh, and that movie made me cry.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.ko: 알리다와 낮추다도 기본형이랑 비교해서 외워야 해요.
dialogue.romanization: allidawa natchudado gibonhyeongirang bigyohaeseo oewoya haeyo.
dialogue.en: You also have to memorize allida and natchuda by comparing them with their base forms.

chapters.guidedPractice: Write five pairs: base action first, causative action second. Example: 아이가 먹어요 -> 엄마가 아이에게 밥을 먹여요.
chapters.realLifeTask: Describe one caregiving, classroom, workplace, or emotion scene using a causative verb and then rewrite it with V-게 하다.
chapters.friendPractice: A partner gives a base verb; answer with a natural causative pair and one full sentence.
chapters.review: Can you tell who does the action and who causes it in 먹다/먹이다, 자다/재우다, 앉다/앉히다, 웃다/웃기다, and 울다/울리다?

beginnerGuide.title: Find the causer
beginnerGuide.body: In 사동 sentences, the subject is often not doing the base action. 엄마가 아이에게 밥을 먹였어요 means the child eats, but the mother causes or helps it happen.

beginnerGuide.title: Learn pairs, not suffix math
beginnerGuide.body: The suffix list is useful, but many causatives are memorized as pairs: 먹다/먹이다, 자다/재우다, 입다/입히다, 앉다/앉히다, 울다/울리다.

beginnerGuide.title: Separate causative and passive
beginnerGuide.body: Some forms look like passive forms, especially 읽히다. Read the whole sentence: 선생님이 학생들에게 본문을 읽혔어요 is causative; 책이 잘 읽혀요 is text-focused/passive-like.

checkpoints: I can identify the causer, the causee, and the base action.
I can produce natural causative pairs without forcing one suffix onto every verb.
I can contrast morphological causative, V-게 하다, and V-게 만들다.

chapters.title: 겠 — Volition, Inference, and Softened Speech
chapters.goal: Use 겠 accurately to express the speaker's volitional intent, confident inference from evidence, and social softening across registers, distinguishing it from -(으)ㄹ 거예요.
chapters.scenario: A waiter promises to bring an order, a scientist infers a result from data, and a colleague politely declines — all three using 겠 for stylistically distinct reasons.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.en: I will check the order right away.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.en: Thank you. Then I will wait a little.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.en: Looking at the data, it looks like the result will change.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.ko: 네, 오늘 회의에서는 설명이 좀 어렵겠습니다.
dialogue.romanization: ne, oneul hoeuieseo-neun seolmyeongi jom eoryeopgetseumnida.
dialogue.en: Yes, in today's meeting, explaining it may be a bit difficult.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.en: I'm sorry, but it will be difficult for me to attend today.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.en: Understood. I will handle this matter.

chapters.guidedPractice: Write two service commitments with -겠습니다, two evidence-based inferences with -겠네요, and one softened refusal with 어렵겠습니다.
chapters.realLifeTask: Practice one customer-service sentence, one data/result inference, and one polite decline using 겠.
chapters.friendPractice: A partner gives a context: service promise, inference, future plan, or soft refusal. Choose 겠, -(으)ㄹ 거예요, or -(으)ㄹ 것 같아요.
chapters.review: Can you explain why 확인하겠습니다, 피곤하시겠네요, and 참석하기 어렵겠습니다 use the same 겠 but do different jobs?

beginnerGuide.title: Separate three jobs
beginnerGuide.body: 겠 can mark a formal commitment, a confident inference, or softened formal speech. Do not translate every 겠 as simple future.

beginnerGuide.title: Service promise
beginnerGuide.body: In service or workplace speech, 확인하겠습니다 and 처리하겠습니다 sound like committed action. 확인할 거예요 sounds more like a plain future plan.

beginnerGuide.title: Inference and refusal
beginnerGuide.body: 피곤하시겠네요 infers from evidence. 참석하기 어렵겠습니다 softens a refusal instead of bluntly saying 못 가요.

checkpoints: I can use -겠습니다 for a formal promise or service action.
I can use -겠네요 for a confident inference from visible evidence or data.
I can distinguish 겠 from -(으)ㄹ 거예요 and -(으)ㄹ 것 같아요.

chapters.title: Unreal Conditionals
chapters.goal: Construct counterfactual conditionals using -았/었으면, -았/었더라면, and -지 않았더라면 to express regret, hypotheticals, and contrary-to-fact wishes.
chapters.scenario: A student reflects on a failed exam, a traveler imagines an alternate route, and a friend expresses what should have been said differently — all requiring counterfactual framing.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.ko: 어제 공지를 미리 알았으면 시험 준비를 더 했을 텐데요.
dialogue.romanization: eoje gongjireul miri arasseumyeon siheom junbireul deo haesseul tendeyo.
dialogue.en: If I had known about the notice in advance yesterday, I would have prepared more for the exam.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.ko: 조금만 일찍 도착했더라면 시험을 볼 수 있었을 거예요.
dialogue.romanization: jogeumman iljjik dochakaetdeoramyeon siheomeul bol su isseosseul geoyeyo.
dialogue.en: If I had arrived just a little earlier, I could have taken the exam.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.ko: 버스를 놓치지 않았더라면 면접에 늦지 않았을 텐데요.
dialogue.romanization: beoseureul notchiji anatdeoramyeon myeonjeobe neutji anatseul tendeyo.
dialogue.en: If I had not missed the bus, I would not have been late for the interview.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.ko: 그때 다른 길로 갔으면 결과가 달라졌을지도 몰라요.
dialogue.romanization: geuttae dareun gillo gasseumyeon gyeolgwaga dallajyeosseuljido mollayo.
dialogue.en: If we had taken a different route then, the result might have changed.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.ko: 친구에게 바로 사과했더라면 지금 이렇게 후회하지 않았을 텐데요.
dialogue.romanization: chinguege baro sagwahaetdeoramyeon jigeum ireoke huhoehaji anatseul tendeyo.
dialogue.en: If I had apologized to my friend right away, I would not regret it like this now.

chapters.guidedPractice: Write one regret about information you did not know, one missed-transport situation, and one relationship regret using -았/었으면 or -았/었더라면.
chapters.realLifeTask: Turn one real regret into a soft Korean sentence such as 미리 알았으면 좋았을 텐데요 or 바로 말했더라면 덜 어색했을 거예요.
chapters.friendPractice: A partner gives a missed condition. Answer with the missed condition first, then a hypothetical result: -았/었더라면 ... -았/었을 거예요.
chapters.review: Can you make both halves hypothetical, instead of mixing a past condition with a plain real result?

beginnerGuide.title: Start from the missed condition
beginnerGuide.body: These sentences begin from something that did not happen: 미리 알다, 일찍 도착하다, 버스를 놓치지 않다, 바로 사과하다.

beginnerGuide.title: Make the result unreal too
beginnerGuide.body: After -았/었으면 or -았/었더라면, the second half usually needs -았/었을 텐데, -았/었을 거예요, or -았/었을지도 몰라요.

beginnerGuide.title: Use -더라면 for stronger hindsight
beginnerGuide.body: -았/었더라면 sounds more reflective and certain that the condition was missed. It fits regret, advice after the fact, and imagining a different outcome.

checkpoints: I can build a regret sentence from a missed past condition.
I can use -지 않았더라면 with the negative before -더라면.
I can choose between a soft wish, -았/었으면 좋겠어요, and a full counterfactual result clause.

chapters.title: Nominalisation — 기 vs 는 것
chapters.goal: Choose correctly between the -기 nominaliser and the -는 것 nominaliser based on semantic weight, definiteness, and grammatical environment.
chapters.scenario: A language tutor explains how to study, a doctor discusses healthy habits, and a journalist describes a recurring event — each requiring a different nominaliser.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.ko: 매일 운동하기는 어렵지만 건강을 위해 필요해요.
dialogue.romanization: maeil undonghagineun eoryeopjiman geongangeul wihae piryohaeyo.
dialogue.en: Exercising every day is hard, but it is necessary for health.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.en: I decided to start with walking first.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.ko: 친구가 매일 걷는 것을 보고 저도 따라 해 보기로 했어요.
dialogue.romanization: chinguga maeil geonneun geoseul bogo jeodo ttara hae bogiro haesseoyo.
dialogue.en: After seeing my friend walk every day, I decided to try following along too.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.ko: 자기 전에 휴대폰 보는 것을 줄이는 것도 목표예요.
dialogue.romanization: jagi jeone hyudaepon boneun geoseul jurineun geotdo mokpyoyeyo.
dialogue.en: Reducing phone-watching before sleeping is also my goal.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.ko: 단어를 외우기 전에 예문을 듣는 게 더 도움이 돼요.
dialogue.romanization: daneoreul oeugi jeone yemuneul deunneun ge deo doumi dwaeyo.
dialogue.en: Listening to example sentences before memorizing words helps more.

chapters.guidedPractice: Write two -기 sentences for tasks or fixed frames, two -는 것 sentences for observed habits, and one 기로 했어요 decision.
chapters.realLifeTask: Describe one habit you want to start or reduce using -기, -는 것, and 기로 했어요.
chapters.friendPractice: A partner gives an action such as 먹다, 듣다, 걷다, or 외우다. Decide whether the sentence needs -기, -는 것, 기 전에, 기 위해, or 기로 했어요.
chapters.review: Can you explain why 운동하기는 어렵다, 친구가 운동하는 것을 봤다, and 운동하기로 했다 use different nominalized forms?

beginnerGuide.title: Use -기 for activity labels
beginnerGuide.body: 운동하기, 공부하기, 걷기 can name an activity as a task, goal, or habit plan. This form is common before 어렵다, 쉽다, 전에, 위해, 시작하다, and 기로 했어요.

beginnerGuide.title: Use -는 것 for a concrete action
beginnerGuide.body: 친구가 걷는 것을 봤어요 and 매일 늦게 먹는 것을 줄이고 있어요 point to an action you see, know, feel, or treat as a concrete habit.

beginnerGuide.title: Memorize the fixed frames
beginnerGuide.body: 기로 했어요, 기 전에, 기 위해서, and 기 시작하다 do not freely switch to -는 것. Learn them as full chunks.

checkpoints: I can use -기 for goals, difficulty, before/for frames, and decisions.
I can use -는 것/거 for a concrete action I see, know, describe, or reduce.
I can avoid replacing fixed forms like 기로 했어요 and 기 전에 with -는 것.

chapters.title: Sentence-Final Attitude Endings
chapters.goal: Deploy the expressive sentence-final endings 네요, 군요/구나, -(으)ㄹ걸요, and -았/었을 텐데 to signal speaker attitude — realisation, surprise, retrospective regret, and unfulfilled expectation.
chapters.scenario: A student just learned something unexpected, a friend wishes a plan had gone differently, and a colleague gently hints they were right all along — all using attitude endings rather than plain statements.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.en: Korean is more fun than I expected.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.ko: 처음에는 어려울 줄 알았는데 생각보다 괜찮군요.
dialogue.romanization: cheoeumeneun eoryeoul jul aranneunde saenggakboda gwaenchanhgunyo.
dialogue.en: I thought it would be hard at first, but it is better than expected.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.en: Oh, they have already arrived.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.en: If you leave now, you will probably be a little late.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.ko: 어제 시간이 있었으면 같이 갔을 텐데요.
dialogue.romanization: eoje sigani isseosseumyeon gachi gasseul tendeyo.
dialogue.en: If I had had time yesterday, I would have gone with you.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.ko: 연습을 많이 했으니까 잘하는 게 당연하네요.
dialogue.romanization: yeonseubeul mani haesseunikka jalhaneun ge dangyeonhaneyo.
dialogue.en: Since you practiced a lot, no wonder you are good.

chapters.guidedPractice: Write one fresh realization with -네요, one formal realization with -군요, one hedged prediction with -ㄹ걸요, and one regret with -았/었을 텐데요.
chapters.realLifeTask: React to one real situation today using the right attitude ending: 놀람이면 -네요/-군요, 예측이면 -ㄹ걸요, 아쉬움이면 -았/었을 텐데요.
chapters.friendPractice: A partner gives you a fact or situation. Choose whether your response should sound like fresh noticing, formal acknowledgement, hedged prediction, or regret.
chapters.review: Can you explain why 재미있네요, 도착하셨군요, 늦을걸요, and 갔을 텐데요 do not have the same speaker attitude?

beginnerGuide.title: Read the speaker's attitude
beginnerGuide.body: These endings do not just add politeness. They tell the listener whether you just noticed something, are acknowledging new information, are guessing, or are regretting a missed outcome.

beginnerGuide.title: Separate noticing from knowing
beginnerGuide.body: -네요 works when the speaker is freshly realizing something. If you already knew it, a plain statement or -잖아요 may fit better.

beginnerGuide.title: Keep regret and prediction apart
beginnerGuide.body: -ㄹ걸요 can hedge a prediction, while -았/었을 텐데요 looks back at a missed past condition. Do not flatten both into English would/probably.

checkpoints: I can use -네요 for fresh realization from what I just noticed.
I can use -군요/구나 for stronger or more formal realization.
I can distinguish -ㄹ걸요 as hedged prediction from -았/었을 텐데요 as regret or unfulfilled expectation.

chapters.title: Topic vs Subject — 은/는 and 이/가
chapters.goal: Choose between 은/는 and 이/가 to correctly signal topic continuity, new information, contrast, emphasis, and exhaustive listing in discourse-level Korean.
chapters.scenario: A narrator introduces a new character, then contrasts two people's opinions, then explains a fact about one of them exclusively — moving through the full topic-subject contrast space.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.en: A friend called.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.en: Does that friend call often?

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.ko: 아니요. 평소에는 메시지를 보내는데 오늘은 제가 먼저 연락했어요.
dialogue.romanization: aniyo. pyeongsoeneun mesijireul bonaeneunde oneureun jega meonjeo yeollakaesseoyo.
dialogue.en: No. Usually they send messages, but today I contacted them first.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.en: Who contacted them first?

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.ko: 제가 먼저 연락했어요. 질문은 쉬웠는데 대답이 어려웠어요.
dialogue.romanization: jega meonjeo yeollakaesseoyo. jilmuneun swiwonneunde daedabi eoryeowosseoyo.
dialogue.en: I contacted them first. The question was easy, but the answer was difficult.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.ko: 그럼 이 문제는 이유가 제일 중요하네요.
dialogue.romanization: geureom i munjeneun iyuga jeil jungyohaneyo.
dialogue.en: Then for this issue, the reason is the most important thing.

chapters.guidedPractice: Write one sentence that introduces new information with 이/가, one that continues a topic with 은/는, one contrast sentence, and one topic-plus-subject sentence.
chapters.realLifeTask: Describe a real message or call today using both particles: 친구가 연락했어요, 그 친구는..., 오늘은 제가...
chapters.friendPractice: A partner asks 누가?, 무엇이?, or 그 사람은? Answer with 이/가 for focused answers and 은/는 for topic or contrast.
chapters.review: Can you explain why 친구가 전화했어요, 그 친구는 자주 전화해요, and 제가 먼저 연락했어요 use different particles?

beginnerGuide.title: New or focused information
beginnerGuide.body: Use 이/가 when the sentence answers who or what, introduces a subject, or points to exactly one answer: 친구가 전화했어요, 제가 먼저 했어요.

beginnerGuide.title: Topic and contrast
beginnerGuide.body: Use 은/는 when the noun is already the topic or when you are contrasting: 그 친구는..., 메시지는 보내지만 전화는 안 해요.

beginnerGuide.title: Frame plus new subject
beginnerGuide.body: Korean can use both in one sentence: 이 문제는 이유가 중요해요. The topic is the frame; 이/가 introduces the important subject inside that frame.

checkpoints: I can use 이/가 for new information, focused answers, and existence predicates.
I can use 은/는 for topic continuity and contrast.
I can build a topic-plus-subject sentence such as 이 문제는 이유가 중요해요.

chapters.title: Advanced Written Korean
chapters.goal: Read and produce formal written Korean using discourse connectors (따라서, 그러나, 반면에, 즉, 결국, 한편) and nominative/copula patterns distinctive to formal prose.
chapters.scenario: Writing a formal complaint, summarising a news article, or composing an essay argument — all requiring the written register that differs substantially from spoken 해요체.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.en: This report lacks evidence.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.en: Therefore, the conclusion must be reviewed again.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.ko: 그러나 핵심 주장은 유지할 수 있습니다.
dialogue.romanization: geureona haeksim jujangeun yujihal su itseumnida.
dialogue.en: However, the main claim can be maintained.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.en: By contrast, the case analysis needs strengthening.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.ko: 한편 예상되는 반론도 따로 검토해야 합니다.
dialogue.romanization: hanpyeon yesangdoeneun ballondo ttaro geomtohaeya hamnida.
dialogue.en: Meanwhile, the expected counterarguments must also be reviewed separately.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.ko: 즉, 결론보다 근거와 논리를 보완해야 합니다.
dialogue.romanization: jeuk, gyeollonboda geungeowa nollireul bowanhaeya hamnida.
dialogue.en: In other words, the evidence and reasoning need more work than the conclusion.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.ko: 결국 보고서는 주장, 근거, 사례가 서로 연결되어야 합니다.
dialogue.romanization: gyeolguk bogoseoneun jujang, geungeo, saryega seoro yeongyeoldoeeoya hamnida.
dialogue.en: Ultimately, a report's claim, evidence, and cases must be connected.

chapters.guidedPractice: Revise a weak report paragraph: add one sentence with 따라서, one contrast with 그러나 or 반면에, one clarification with 즉, and one final synthesis with 결국.
chapters.realLifeTask: Summarise a short article, notice, or team-project issue in four formal sentences using at least two written connectors.
chapters.friendPractice: A partner gives you a claim and two pieces of evidence; decide whether the conclusion, evidence, logic, or counterargument needs revision.
chapters.review: Can you explain why 따라서, 그러나, 반면에, 한편, 즉, and 결국 cannot be swapped freely in a formal paragraph?

beginnerGuide.title: Register first
beginnerGuide.body: This chapter is about written reasoning, not casual conversation. A paragraph with 따라서 or 그러나 should usually keep formal endings such as -다, -한다, -이다, or formal polite -습니다.

beginnerGuide.title: Connector roles
beginnerGuide.body: Use 따라서 for a conclusion from evidence, 그러나 for direct contrast, 반면에 for two-sided comparison, 한편 for a parallel development, 즉 for restatement, and 결국 for final synthesis.

beginnerGuide.title: Argument vocabulary
beginnerGuide.body: Read 근거, 결론, 핵심, 논리, 사례, and 반론 as one set. These words let you diagnose what is weak in a report instead of only saying the Korean is difficult.

checkpoints: I can choose 따라서, 그러나, 반면에, 한편, 즉, or 결국 according to the relationship between sentences.
I can revise a report sentence using 근거, 결론, 핵심, 논리, 사례, and 반론.
I can keep formal written connectors and written-register endings consistent in one paragraph.

chapters.title: Korean Internet Language and Colloquial Intensifiers
chapters.goal: Recognise and appropriately use Korean internet abbreviations, phonetic shortenings, and colloquial intensifiers in informal digital communication while understanding their register constraints.
chapters.scenario: Reading a social media comment thread, replying to a friend's message on KakaoTalk, and understanding a streaming chat during a live broadcast.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.ko: 그 댓글 봤어? 완전 웃겨 ㅋㅋㅋ.
dialogue.romanization: geu daetgeul bwasseo? wanjeon utgyeo kkk.
dialogue.en: Did you see that comment? It's so funny lol.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.en: Yeah, I saw it. Whoa, did you hit like?

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.ko: 응, 친구한테 공유했어. 댓글 반응도 레전드야.
dialogue.romanization: eung, chinguhante gongyuhaesseo. daetgeul baneungdo rejeondeuya.
dialogue.en: Yeah, I shared it with a friend. The comment reactions are legendary too.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.ko: 공식 글에는 ㅋㅋ 빼고 재미있었습니다처럼 써야 해.
dialogue.romanization: gongsik geureneneun kk ppaego jaemiisseotseumnidacheoreom sseoya hae.
dialogue.en: In an official post, you should leave out ㅋㅋ and write something like 'it was interesting.'

chapters.guidedPractice: Rewrite five casual chat reactions for two settings: friend chat with ㅋㅋ/ㅇㅇ/완전, then official writing without slang.
chapters.realLifeTask: Read a comment thread or live chat and sort three expressions into safe with friends, safe in polite chat, and avoid in formal writing.
chapters.friendPractice: A partner names a relationship: close friend, classmate, professor, company account, or livestream chat. Choose the reaction that fits the register.
chapters.review: Can you explain when ㅋㅋ, ㅠㅠ, ㅇㅇ, ㄹㅇ, ㅇㅈ, 대박, 완전, 레전드, and 개웃겨 are natural and when to replace them?

beginnerGuide.title: Register first
beginnerGuide.body: This chapter is about relationship and channel. ㅋㅋ and ㅇㅇ can be perfect in a friend chat and still be rude or careless in an email, professor message, or company notice.

beginnerGuide.title: Reaction families
beginnerGuide.body: Read the forms as families: ㅋㅋ/ㅠㅠ for emotion, ㅇㅇ/ㅇㅈ/ㄹㅇ for agreement or truth, and 완전/진짜/대박/레전드/개웃겨 for intensity.

beginnerGuide.title: Platform actions
beginnerGuide.body: Match digital nouns with their natural verbs: 댓글을 달다, 좋아요를 누르다, 친구한테 공유하다, 라이브 채팅에 올라오다.

checkpoints: I can recognize ㅋㅋ, ㅠㅠ, ㅇㅇ, ㄹㅇ, and ㅇㅈ and explain their register limits.
I can use 완전, 진짜, 대박, 레전드, and 개웃겨 with friends while avoiding them in formal writing.
I can pair 댓글, 좋아요, 공유하다, and 라이브 채팅 with natural Korean verbs.

chapters.title: Synthesis and Production Review
chapters.goal: Demonstrate mastery of all patterns ch1–64 through integrated production tasks spanning multiple registers, domains, and grammar points simultaneously.
chapters.scenario: A learner prepares for a job interview in Korea, writes a formal email, has a casual conversation with coworkers, and sends a casual KakaoTalk message — all in the same day, switching registers appropriately.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.ko: 오늘 면접 답변, 이메일, 카톡 답장을 한 번에 검수해 볼까요?
dialogue.romanization: oneul myeonjeop dapbyeon, imeil, katok dapjangeul han beone geomsuhae bolkkayo?
dialogue.en: Shall we review today's interview answer, email, and KakaoTalk reply together?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.ko: 먼저 상황과 상대방을 정하고 문체를 맞춰야 해요.
dialogue.romanization: meonjeo sanghwanggwa sangdaebangeul jeonghago munchereul matchwoya haeyo.
dialogue.en: First, decide the situation and listener, then match the style.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.ko: 면접 답변은 높임말과 시제를 확인하고, 이메일은 연결어와 마무리를 봐요.
dialogue.romanization: myeonjeop dapbyeoneun nopimmalgwa sijereul hwaginhago, imeireun yeongyeoreowa mamurireul bwayo.
dialogue.en: For the interview answer, check honorifics and tense; for the email, check connectors and the closing.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.ko: 카톡에서는 편하게 써도 되지만 회사 메일에는 ㅋㅋ를 빼야 해요.
dialogue.romanization: katogeseoneun pyeonhage sseodo doejiman hoesa meileneun kkreul ppaeya haeyo.
dialogue.en: You can write casually in KakaoTalk, but in a company email you need to remove ㅋㅋ.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.en: Lastly, I will check even each particle again.

chapters.guidedPractice: Choose one idea and produce it four ways: interview answer, formal email, coworker chat, and friend KakaoTalk. Check situation, listener, style, particles, tense, and connectors each time.
chapters.realLifeTask: Before sending one Korean message today, run the five-layer checklist: purpose, listener, register/style, grammar accuracy, and closing.
chapters.friendPractice: A partner gives you a task and relationship. Say whether you need casual, polite, or formal Korean, then produce and revise one sentence.
chapters.review: Can you switch the same message between interview, email, coworker talk, and friend chat without leaving mismatched particles, tense, connectors, or slang?

beginnerGuide.title: Start with the situation
beginnerGuide.body: Do not start by translating English. First decide the purpose, listener, and channel: interview, email, coworker chat, or friend KakaoTalk.

beginnerGuide.title: Check five layers
beginnerGuide.body: After drafting, check 문체, 입자, 시제, 높임말, and 연결어. A sentence can have good vocabulary and still fail because one layer does not match the situation.

beginnerGuide.title: Rewrite, not decorate
beginnerGuide.body: Polite Korean is not casual Korean with 요 added. Rewrite rough slang, sentence endings, connectors, and closing phrases together.

checkpoints: I can decide the register before choosing vocabulary or endings.
I can check 입자, 시제, 문체, 높임말, and 연결어 in one sentence.
I can rewrite the same idea for a formal email, interview answer, coworker chat, and friend KakaoTalk.
